TOYS McCOY Men's MA-1 Flight Jacket, ALBERT TURNER MIL-J-8279A Reproduction, Nylon Twill Shell, Wool Pile Interlining, Made in Japan (TMJ2640, Sage)

TOYS McCOY

This men's Type MA-1 flight jacket is made in Japan by TOYS McCOY. The design reproduces a 1950s U.S. Air Force jacket manufactured by ALBERT TURNER & CO., INC. to the MIL-J-8279A specification, focusing on the early configuration with a square-topped internal wind flap. Its construction combines a gray-toned Sage nylon twill shell, a full nylon lining, wool pile interlining on a cotton base fabric, and wool rib-knit trim at the collar, cuffs, and waistband. A nylon oxygen-mask hose tab, snap-fastened ICS communication-cord loops, flapless waist pockets, a zippered sleeve utility pocket, and U.S. Air Force markings reproduce the equipment-related details and appearance of the early MA-1. The substantial interlining adds warmth and volume through the body and sleeves, while the short body length and rib-knit waistband create the rounded silhouette associated with this classic flight jacket. Together, these materials and structural details bring the character of the original military garment into a reproduction suited to contemporary casual wear.

Size and Fit Guide:

Gender: Men.

This jacket has a classic MA-1 fit, with room through the chest and body and a comparatively short body length. The generous body width is drawn in at the waist by the rib-knit waistband, creating a rounded upper-body silhouette with a defined lower edge. The insulating interlining between the shell and lining also gives the body and sleeves more thickness and volume than an L-2-series light-zone flight jacket without an insulating interlining.

The thickness of the interlining affects the space available inside the jacket, so it may fit differently from a thinner jacket with the same flat chest-width measurement. The thickness of the clothing worn underneath, your body type, and your preferred fit will also affect how it feels when worn. Before selecting a size, please measure a similar flight jacket that fits you well, preferably one with comparable thickness and construction, and compare its chest width, body length, center-back sleeve length, sleeve length from the shoulder seam, and shoulder width with the measurements below.

1950s ALBERT TURNER MIL-J-8279A Reproduction
This model reproduces an early Type MA-1 flight jacket made for the U.S. Air Force by ALBERT TURNER & CO., INC. under the MIL-J-8279A specification. The A specification was the first revision of the original MA-1 specification, and this reproduction specifically follows the configuration with a square upper end on the internal wind flap.

The reproduction brings together the gray-toned Sage Green shell, wool pile interlining, square-topped wind flap, nylon oxygen-mask hose tab, snap-fastened communication-cord loops, flapless waist pockets, left-sleeve utility pocket, and Air Force markings. These details identify the particular early configuration being reproduced and connect its appearance to the practical equipment requirements of the original jacket.

MA-1 Development and Specification Revisions
The Type MA-1 emerged in the 1950s from the development of the Type B-15 flight-jacket series and remained in use among U.S. military aviation personnel and ground crews through successive specification revisions. The original MIL-J-8279 specification was followed by MIL-J-8279A, MIL-J-8279B, MIL-J-8279C, MIL-J-8279D, MIL-J-8279E, MIL-J-8279F, and MIL-J-8279G, with the jacket's construction changing as flight conditions, equipment, and operational requirements evolved.

Differences between specifications include the shape of the internal wind flap, equipment tabs and cord loops, lining arrangements, pocket construction, and provisions for reversible wear. Jackets with a similar overall appearance can therefore differ in their exterior details, equipment attachment points, and internal construction according to their production period, specification, and contractor. This model reproduces the early arrangement with a square-topped wind flap and equipment-related tabs and loops.

The low rib-knit collar also reflects the relationship between flight clothing and aviation equipment. Modified examples of the B-15 series replaced the large mouton collar with a knitted collar to accommodate changing equipment. The MA-1 likewise uses a low knit collar that helps reduce interference around helmets and other gear.

High-Density 100% Nylon Twill Shell in Gray-Toned Sage Green
The shell is made from 100% nylon twill woven at a high density. The closely woven fabric has a smooth, compact surface and a substantial hand, combining noticeable thickness with the flexibility needed to bend and move with the garment.

The fabric develops a restrained sheen as the direction of the light and the viewing angle change. These shifting highlights and shadows give definition to the folds and rounded volume of the jacket without obscuring the underlying weave. The Sage Green color has a gray cast, giving the shell its muted, subdued appearance.

Full 100% Nylon Lining Through the Body and Sleeves
The jacket is fully lined with 100% nylon fabric through both the body and sleeves. This smooth inner surface sits between the wearer's clothing and the insulating interlining enclosed within the jacket.

The smooth nylon reduces friction against the layers worn underneath, helping the jacket slide on and off and limiting catching as the arms move. The lining therefore contributes to ease of wear while covering the insulation throughout the body and sleeves.

100% Wool Pile Interlining on a 100% Cotton Base Fabric
An insulating pile interlining is enclosed between the nylon shell and nylon lining. Its pile is made from 100% wool, while the supporting base fabric is 100% cotton. These percentages refer to the two components separately: the wool forms the raised pile, and the cotton forms the fabric that supports it.

The interlining extends through the body and sleeves. Air held within the wool pile contributes to an insulating layer between the outer shell and the smooth inner lining, helping the jacket retain warmth.

The physical depth of the pile also gives the garment thickness and volume. This internal structure supports the rounded shape of the body and sleeves, making the interlining part of both the jacket's thermal construction and its characteristic MA-1 silhouette.

Front Zipper with T.McCOY-Marked Slider and Leather Pull Tab
The front closes with a zipper fitted with a metal slider marked "T.McCOY" and a loop-shaped metal pull. A leather tab is attached to the metal pull, extending the area available to grip when opening or closing the jacket.

The leather provides a flexible handle that can be held between the fingers, making the pull easier to grasp and helping with operation of the front zipper. The metal slider, loop-shaped pull, and leather extension form distinct components of the closure.

Square-Topped Internal Wind Flap with Zigzag Stitching
A vertical wind flap, also called a storm flap, runs behind the front zipper on the wearer's right front panel. Positioned inside the closure, it provides a backing layer behind the zipper and helps reduce drafts entering through the front opening.

The upper end of the flap is square, reproducing the shape used in the early MA-1 configuration on which this jacket is based. This outline is a specific detail of the design source, alongside the equipment tabs and flapless waist pockets.

Zigzag stitching secures the interlining inside the flap. The stitching helps hold the insulating material in position and reduces its tendency to shift or gather within the flap, while also creating the visible zigzag pattern on its surface.

Flapless, Snap-Fastened Single-Welt Waist Pockets
The front has one waist pocket on each side, with the openings set at an angle. Each opening is finished with a single welt and can be secured with a snap fastener. There is no separate exterior flap covering the pocket entrance.

This arrangement preserves the flapless waist-pocket construction of the early MA-1 being reproduced. The angled openings form a clearly defined detail on the lower front, while the snaps allow the entrances to be fastened closed. The pocket bags are made from brushed double-face fabric, giving the pocket interiors a different texture from the smooth nylon shell and body lining.

Two Interior Pockets with Cotton Drill Pocket Bags
There is one interior pocket on each front panel. Both have vertically oriented openings that can be closed with snap fasteners, providing storage inside the jacket as well as at the exterior waist.

Cotton drill is used for the interior pocket bags. These bags form the storage compartments behind the pocket openings and are separate from the nylon lining that covers the body and sleeves. Their material also differs from the brushed double-face fabric used for the exterior waist-pocket bags.

Left-Sleeve Utility Pocket with TALON Zipper and Four Pen Slots
A zippered utility pocket is positioned on the left upper sleeve. Often called a cigarette pocket, this is a characteristic detail of U.S. military nylon flight jackets. The main compartment closes with a TALON zipper, whose metal pull is fitted with a leather tab to make it easier to grasp.

The outside of the pocket also incorporates four individual pen slots. These narrow compartments separate the pens from one another and from the main zippered storage area, combining two types of storage within the sleeve-pocket assembly.

U.S. Air Force Marking Printed on the Left Sleeve
Above the utility pocket, the left sleeve carries a U.S. Air Force wing-and-star emblem together with the wording "U.S. AIR FORCE." The design is printed directly onto the nylon shell, so the marking sits on the garment fabric rather than on a separately attached patch.

Nylon Oxygen-Mask Hose Tab at the Left Chest
A nylon oxygen-mask hose tab is attached vertically beside the front zipper on the wearer's left chest. Its color is similar to that of the shell, allowing the equipment detail to blend into the Sage Green front panel while remaining visible through its shape and placement.

On the original jacket, this tab provided a point for clipping an oxygen-mask hose in place. The reproduction retains the structure of this equipment attachment detail as part of its early MA-1 configuration.

Snap-Fastened ICS Communication-Cord Loops
The jacket has snap-fastened ICS communication-cord loops at both sides of the body. The snap closures allow each loop to be opened and fastened around a cord, reflecting the practical construction of the original equipment detail.

On the original design, these loops were used to retain wiring associated with headsets, microphones, and the aircraft's communication system. Their presence complements the oxygen-mask hose tab and reproduces the equipment-related features of this early specification.

100% Wool Rib-Knit Trim and Low Knit Collar
The collar, cuffs, and waistband are all made from 100% wool rib knit. The knitted structure provides flexibility and stretch at the jacket's neck, wrist, and waist openings, allowing these areas to follow the body while the nylon shell retains its fuller shape.

At the neckline, the low collar follows the neck without the height or bulk of a large mouton collar. Its flexible construction helps accommodate neck and shoulder movement, while the closer fit around the opening helps reduce the entry of wind.

Stepped Rib-Knit Cuffs with Two Rib Textures
The cuffs use a stepped rib-knit construction in which the rib pattern changes partway along the cuff. The section adjoining the nylon sleeve has wider ribs, while the section toward the wrist opening has finer ribs. This creates a visible transition in the knitted texture within each cuff.

The stretch of the wool knit allows the cuffs to sit comfortably around the wrists and helps limit drafts entering through the sleeve openings. Drawing the full nylon sleeves inward at the wrists also helps hold the sleeve ends in position and gives the sleeves their rounded volume above the cuffs.

Rib-Knit Waistband and Rounded MA-1 Silhouette
The bottom of the jacket is finished with a wool rib-knit waistband. Its stretch draws the comparatively roomy body inward at the waist, giving the lower edge a closer fit than the chest and upper body.

The resulting shape comes from the combination of a short body, room through the chest, the volume of the internal insulation, and the narrowing effect of the waistband. These elements work together to create the rounded, waist-length silhouette associated with the MA-1 flight jacket.

Reproduction ALBERT TURNER Contractor Label
A reproduction ALBERT TURNER & CO., INC. contractor label is sewn inside the back neckline. Its wording includes "JACKET, FLYING, MAN'S, INTERMEDIATE," "TYPE MA-1," "SPEC. MIL-J-8279A," "ORDER NO. AF 33(602)-8077," and "ALBERT TURNER & CO., INC."

These markings reproduce the garment designation, type, specification number, order number, and contractor identification found on the military label being recreated. The label records the historical design source represented by this TOYS McCOY reproduction.

White U.S. Air Force Marking Inside the Back Neckline
Below the contractor label, a U.S. Air Force wing-and-star emblem and the words "U.S. AIR FORCE" are printed in white directly onto the lining. This places a second Air Force marking inside the jacket, in addition to the marking on the left sleeve.

The interior print is normally hidden when the jacket is worn. Reproducing it beneath the label carries the early MA-1 detailing into the back-neck lining as well as the exterior shell.

Made in Japan
TOYS McCOY model TMJ2640 is made in Japan as a reproduction of the ALBERT TURNER & CO., INC. MIL-J-8279A configuration. Its gray-toned Sage Green nylon twill, wool pile interlining, and wool rib-knit trim establish the material character and rounded shape of the jacket.

The square-topped wind flap, flapless waist pockets, sleeve utility pocket, oxygen-mask hose tab, communication-cord loops, contractor label, and Air Force markings complete the early specification being recreated. Together, the fabric, insulation, and construction details preserve the practical character of the original design in a flight jacket for everyday casual wear.

Care Instructions
Do not wash at home.
Do not use chlorine bleach or oxygen bleach.
Do not tumble dry.
Do not iron.
Do not dry clean.
Do not professionally wet clean.
Consult a specialist cleaner for advice on appropriate care.

Always follow the care instructions attached to the actual product. When consulting a specialist, show them the care label so they can assess an appropriate method for this jacket.

Additional Precautions for Care and Handling

Protecting the Jacket’s Shape
Water and heat can cause wool insulation, rib-knit components, and leather details to shrink or become distorted, affecting the jacket’s overall shape. Do not soak, wash, or tumble dry this jacket.

Protecting the Air Force Marking
Dry-cleaning solvents may fade or completely remove heat-transfer Air Force markings. Do not dry clean this jacket.

Localized Stain Treatment
For localized stains, consult a specialist about whether gentle wiping with a cloth dampened with a diluted mild, pH-neutral detergent is appropriate. Spot treatment may cause uneven coloration, so any proposed method should first be tested in an inconspicuous area. Always follow the jacket’s actual care label.

Avoid Artificial Distressing
Do not deliberately soil or distress the jacket to create a worn appearance, as this may damage the fabric or components.

Important Notes
- Our inventory is shared among our physical retail store and multiple online stores, so inventory changes may not always be reflected immediately on each website.
- Even after an order has been placed, an item may occasionally be sold out due to the timing of simultaneous purchases. We sincerely appreciate your understanding.
- All measurements are taken manually with the garment laid flat, using a measuring tape.
- Because individual garments and measuring methods may vary, slight measurement differences may occur.
- The actual color of the product may appear slightly different from the photographs depending on lighting conditions and the settings of your monitor or display.

Barns Outfitters Men's COZUN Vintage-Inspired Long-Sleeve Zip-Up Hoodie, Medium-Weight 100% Cotton Brushed Fleece, Hooded Sweatshirt with a Two-Way Zipper, Flatseam Construction, One-Wash, Made in Japan (BR-3010 RD)

BARNS OUTFITTERS

See available colors here

This men's long-sleeve zip-up hoodie is made in Japan by Barns Outfitters as part of its COZUN series. Drawing on the practical construction of classic American athletic wear and vintage sweatshirts, the design brings together carefully developed fabric, knitting, stitching, and functional garment details. Its medium-weight 100% cotton sweatshirt fabric is knitted on COZUN small-diameter knitting machines. These machines are modified versions of older sinker knitting machines that were used during the transition from traditional loopwheel machines to high-speed sinker knitting machines. The name COZUN comes from the Japanese term for these small-diameter machines. By knitting slowly while limiting tension on the yarn and the developing fabric, this process produces a soft, supple hand together with moderate firmness and body. This balance gives the fabric a comfortable, yielding feel while providing enough structure to support the hoodie's outline. The reverse is brushed to create a soft, full interior, with the raised cotton fibers holding air and contributing to warmth. A two-way front zipper, double-layer hood, rib-knit underarm gussets, extended cuffs and waistband, and visible flatseam stitching give the plain design its distinctive character. The one-wash finish further softens the initial feel while preserving the fabric's underlying body. A slightly slim silhouette keeps excess volume to a minimum, allowing the hoodie to work as an everyday outer layer or beneath a jacket. Together, the distinctive COZUN fabric and practical construction details bring the character of vintage athletic clothing into contemporary casual wear.

Size and Fit Guide:

Gender: Men.

The hoodie has a slightly slim, streamlined fit, with a body that does not flare outward and relatively close-cut armholes. It follows the body naturally while retaining moderate ease, limiting excess fabric through the torso and sleeves. The body length is moderate rather than especially cropped, giving it proportions that work with both casual outfits and a cleaner, more put-together style.

Set-in sleeves create a defined shoulder line. The deep rib-knit waistband draws the lower body inward only gently, allowing the fabric to fall naturally from the torso to the hem without a strongly cinched waist. Extended rib-knit cuffs provide a comfortable fit around the wrists. The relatively restrained volume also makes the hoodie suitable for layering under a jacket or coat.

Fit will vary with your body type, the thickness of the clothing worn underneath, and your preferred amount of ease. Please measure a similar sweatshirt or zip-up hoodie that fits you well and compare its chest width, body length, center-back sleeve length, sleeve length from the shoulder seam, and shoulder width with the measurements below. When comparing with another zip-up hoodie, please close its front zipper before laying it flat to measure.

The knitted fabric has natural give, and the rib-knit underarm gussets, cuffs, and waistband stretch with movement. The listed measurements describe the garment laid flat, so please consider this flexibility along with the measurements when choosing your size.

Classic American Athletic-Wear Construction
The design takes its starting point from the practical construction of classic American athletic wear and vintage sweatshirts. The emphasis is on the relationship between the fabric, garment panels, rib-knit components, and stitching. The plain exterior allows the knitted texture, panel junctions, and functional details to remain visible without relying on added decoration.

The two-way zipper provides adjustable front coverage, while the double-layer hood, underarm gussets, and extended rib-knit finishes give each opening and junction a specific role. These details are combined with a relatively streamlined silhouette, preserving the familiar character of a traditional sweatshirt hoodie in proportions suited to everyday casual wear.

COZUN Small-Diameter Knitting
The sweatshirt fabric is knitted on a COZUN small-diameter knitting machine. The name COZUN comes from the Japanese term for this type of small-diameter machine. Its construction is based on a modified older sinker knitting machine of the type used during the transition from loopwheel machines to modern high-speed sinker knitting equipment.

The fabric is knitted slowly while limiting tension on the yarn and the developing knit. This process produces a soft hand together with moderate firmness and body. The softness allows the material to settle comfortably against the wearer, while its underlying structure helps support the outline of the hoodie.

Medium-Weight 100% Cotton Sweatshirt Fabric with 30/7 Yarn Construction
The fabric is a medium-weight sweatshirt knit made from 100% cotton. It has a moderate thickness and a soft feel, balancing substance with flexibility. The construction uses No. 30 cotton yarn on the face and thicker No. 7 cotton yarn on the reverse. The relatively fine face yarn forms the more finely textured outer surface, while the thicker backing yarn contributes fullness to the interior.

Fine columns of knit stitches run vertically along the face. Slight variations in the knitted surface and the natural fuzz of the cotton give the fabric a subtle, irregular texture reminiscent of vintage sweatshirts. This surface character comes from the yarn and knitting rather than an added printed pattern.

Soft Brushed Interior
The reverse of the sweatshirt fabric is brushed to raise the cotton fibers into a soft, full surface. This gives the inside a cushioned feel against the body and distinguishes it from an unbrushed sweatshirt knit.

The raised fibers create small spaces that hold air within the brushed surface, contributing to warmth. The resulting fabric combines a relatively fine outer face with a fuller interior, maintaining the moderate overall thickness of a medium-weight sweatshirt.

One-Wash Finish
The hoodie is washed once during finishing. This initial wash softens the fabric's crispness while retaining moderate body, giving it a more settled feel from the first wear. Compared with an unwashed garment, it is less prone to substantial initial shrinkage because it has already undergone a wash before sale.

The finish does not eliminate the possibility of further dimensional change. As a 100% cotton knitted garment, it may still shrink slightly or change in size depending on subsequent washing and drying conditions and differences between individual garments. With continued wear and washing, the fabric gradually settles further and develops a more naturally worn-in texture.

Two-Way Front Zipper
The front uses a two-way zipper with two sliders. Once the zipper is fastened, the upper slider allows the opening at the chest and neckline to be adjusted, while the lower slider allows the front to open upward from the hem.

Opening the lower section slightly when seated gives the fabric more room around the abdomen and hips. This can reduce tightness and pulling in the lower body, improving comfort and limiting strain on the fabric where it would otherwise be drawn taut.

The lower opening also allows part of an underlying shirt to show while the upper section remains closed. The two sliders therefore provide control over both the way the hoodie sits on the body and the appearance of the front opening.

Double-Layer Hood with a Center Seam and No Drawcord
The hood uses two layers of the same sweatshirt fabric as the body. The layers are arranged so that the fabric's face is visible on both the outside and the inside of the hood. The brushed reverse surfaces sit between the layers, leaving the finer knitted face exposed on either side.

The left and right hood sections are joined along a vertical center seam to create a shaped, three-dimensional form. The combined thickness of the two layers and the center seam help support the hood's outline, allowing it to stand naturally around the back of the neck and retain a defined shape.

The opening is made without a drawcord. This keeps the front edge visually simple, allowing the doubled fabric and shaped construction to define the hood's appearance.

Set-In Sleeves with One-Piece Sleeve Bodies
The long sleeves use a set-in construction, with each sleeve cap sewn into the corresponding armhole in the body. The resulting shoulder and armhole seams define the transition between the torso and sleeve, giving the upper body a neat outline.

Each main sleeve section is made from a single fabric panel whose edges are joined along the underside of the arm to form a tube. This lengthwise underarm seam closes the sleeve body, while the cuff is attached as a separate rib-knit component at the wrist.

Stretch Rib-Knit Underarm Gussets
A separate rib-knit gusset is inserted at each underarm where the sleeve joins the body. The gusset is sewn to the surrounding panels, creating a section of more flexible fabric at the sleeve attachment.

As the arms are raised or extended forward, the rib knit stretches with the movement. This helps ease pulling around the base of the sleeve and supplements freedom of movement through the armhole. Its role is particularly useful in a hoodie with relatively close-cut armholes, where a flexible junction helps accommodate movement without adding broad overall volume.

Extended Double-Layer Rib-Knit Cuffs
The cuffs use rib knit produced separately from the main sweatshirt fabric. Each cuff is folded back on itself to form a double layer, then sewn to the end of the sleeve. The folded construction gives the wrist opening a defined edge, while the rib knit provides stretch.

The knit becomes finer toward the cuff edge from the seam where the cuff meets the sleeve. Together with the elasticity of the rib structure, this helps the cuff conform comfortably around the wrist.

The cuffs are longer than those commonly found on standard sweatshirts, covering a greater area around the wrists. Their close, flexible fit helps limit the entry of cold air through the sleeve openings, while their extended proportions contribute to the hoodie's vintage athletic-wear appearance.

Deep Double-Layer Rib-Knit Waistband
The lower body is finished with a comparatively deep rib-knit waistband. As with the cuffs, the rib knit is folded into a double layer and sewn to the main sweatshirt body, creating a substantial but flexible lower edge.

The waistband has greater stretch than the main fabric, allowing it to follow the waist and help the hem sit securely. Its inward pull is restrained, so it does not strongly cinch the lower body. Instead, the silhouette falls naturally from the torso toward the hem, preserving the hoodie's relatively clean, straight-looking lower profile.

Split Kangaroo-Style Patch Pockets
Two kangaroo-style patch pockets sit at the lower front, one on each side of the zipper. Each pocket is made from a separate piece of the same sweatshirt fabric, laid over and stitched to the outside of the body. The space between the pocket panel and the body forms the storage compartment.

The left and right pockets are separate compartments. Each has an angled opening at its outer side, positioned to allow the hand to enter naturally from the side. In addition to holding small items, the pockets can be used as hand warmers.

The edges of the openings are turned back and secured with stitching. This reinforces the pocket mouths where repeated hand entry places stress on the fabric. The openings are relatively broad, so please take care that items do not fall out.

The inner edges follow the line of the front zipper, and the lower edges extend to the junction between the body and the rib-knit waistband. Their symmetrical placement and slanted openings create the recognizable front arrangement associated with classic athletic hoodies.

Flatseamer Construction for Low-Profile Seams
The main components are joined with flatlock seams sewn on a flatseamer. Compared with constructions that leave raised seam allowances on the inside, this method keeps the junctions relatively flat and limits abrupt changes in thickness where the fabric sections meet.

Controlling these junctions helps reduce bulky ridges against the body at sewn areas such as the sides, shoulders, armholes, underarm gussets, sleeve undersides, cuffs, pockets, and waistband. The construction allows the sweatshirt to retain its fabric thickness while keeping the seams less prominent against the wearer.

The cuffs use rib knit produced separately from the main sweatshirt fabric. Each cuff is folded back on itself to form a double layer, then sewn to the end of the sleeve. The folded construction gives the wrist opening a defined edge, while the rib knit provides stretch.

The knit becomes finer toward the cuff edge from the seam where the cuff meets the sleeve. Together with the elasticity of the rib structure, this helps the cuff conform comfortably around the wrist.

The cuffs are longer than those commonly found on standard sweatshirts, covering a greater area around the wrists. Their close, flexible fit helps limit the entry of cold air through the sleeve openings, while their extended proportions contribute to the hoodie's vintage athletic-wear appearance.

Deep Double-Layer Rib-Knit Waistband
The lower body is finished with a comparatively deep rib-knit waistband. As with the cuffs, the rib knit is folded into a double layer and sewn to the main sweatshirt body, creating a substantial but flexible lower edge.

The waistband has greater stretch than the main fabric, allowing it to follow the waist and help the hem sit securely. Its inward pull is restrained, so it does not strongly cinch the lower body. Instead, the silhouette falls naturally from the torso toward the hem, preserving the hoodie's relatively clean, straight-looking lower profile.

Split Kangaroo-Style Patch Pockets
Two kangaroo-style patch pockets sit at the lower front, one on each side of the zipper. Each pocket is made from a separate piece of the same sweatshirt fabric, laid over and stitched to the outside of the body. The space between the pocket panel and the body forms the storage compartment.

The edges of the openings are turned back and secured with stitching. This reinforces the pocket mouths where repeated hand entry places stress on the fabric. The openings are relatively broad, so please take care that items do not fall out.

The inner edges follow the line of the front zipper, and the lower edges extend to the junction between the body and the rib-knit waistband. Their symmetrical placement and slanted openings create the recognizable front arrangement associated with classic athletic hoodies.

Controlling these junctions helps reduce bulky ridges against the body at sewn areas such as the sides, shoulders, armholes, underarm gussets, sleeve undersides, cuffs, pockets, and waistband. The flatseam stitching also forms part of the exterior design. Stitch lines remain visible along the component junctions, outlining the changes between the body panels, sleeves, gussets, rib-knit sections, and pockets.

On the plain design, these lines provide a restrained visual accent while making the construction easier to see. The appearance comes from the stitching used to assemble the garment, linking its decorative effect directly to the structure of the hoodie.

Made in Japan

The adjustable two-way zipper and relatively streamlined fit make it practical as an everyday outer layer or beneath a jacket or coat. With minimal added decoration, its character comes from the pigment-dyed finish, knitting, stitching, and construction of the individual parts.

14.8 oz. Extra Heavyweight 100% Cotton Sweatshirt Fabric
The sweatshirt is made from 14.8 oz. extra heavyweight fabric knitted from 100% cotton. The material has substantial thickness and a distinctly weighty feel, giving the body and sleeves a firm, full-bodied structure even before the garment has been washed.

Fine vertical columns of knit stitches are visible on the outer surface. The natural character of the yarn and slight irregularities in the knitted surface give the face a subtly uneven texture, recalling the straightforward appearance of vintage athletic sweatshirts.

Brushed Reverse for Warmth
The reverse of the sweatshirt fabric is brushed to raise a soft layer of fibers on the inside. This gives the inner surface a different texture from the more clearly defined knit stitches visible on the exterior.

The raised fibers hold air close to the body, while the thickness of the underlying knit provides additional substance. Together, the brushed reverse and heavyweight construction contribute to the fabric's insulating character. The warmth comes from the sweatshirt fabric itself and its brushed inner surface.

Circular-Knit Tubular Body Without Side Seams
The torso is knitted as a continuous tube on a circular knitting machine. This tubular construction creates a body without vertical seams running down either side, avoiding the separate front-to-back joins used along the sides of many cut-and-sewn tops.

Because there are no side seams, there are also no corresponding seam allowances or overlapping fabric edges along the sides of the torso. This is particularly useful with a fabric of this thickness, as it limits the extra bulk and raised ridges that could otherwise form where the front and back panels meet. The construction leaves a smooth, uninterrupted transition around the sides of the body.

Unwashed Finish and Changes Through Laundering
The completed garment has not been washed during production. In this unwashed state, the extra heavyweight cotton knit already has a firm, substantial hand, with enough body to give the sweatshirt a defined outline.

As the cotton and knitted structure settle and contract through laundering, the stitches draw closer together and the fabric becomes more compact. Its feel develops toward a denser, more substantial texture while retaining the natural suppleness of cotton. This change in density is part of the way the unwashed knit develops with washing.

The same process can affect the garment's dimensions. Width tends to show comparatively little change, while body length may shorten slightly. This is a tendency rather than a fixed shrinkage allowance, and the amount of dimensional change will depend on washing and drying conditions. Warm or hot water and machine drying can encourage greater shrinkage or distortion, so please hand wash gently according to the attached care label, reshape, and air dry in the shade.

Rib-Knit Binder Crew Neck with Double Stitching
The crew neck is finished with a separate rib-knit binding that wraps around the cut edge of the body fabric. The binding encloses the neckline edge from both the outside and inside, holding the cut edge between its folded sections.

Two rows of stitching secure the binding to the body. This arrangement reinforces the neckline on both faces and supports the edge as the opening stretches during dressing and undressing.

The combination of the surrounding rib-knit binding and double stitching helps limit stretching out, waviness, and distortion at the neck. It provides a supported opening that is better able to retain its defined crew-neck shape through repeated wear.

Double-Layer V Inserts at the Front and Back
A V-shaped rib-knit insert is positioned below the neckline on both the front and back. Often described as a double-V detail, this arrangement gives the sweatshirt the characteristic inset construction associated with vintage athletic wear when viewed from either direction.

Each insert is made from V-shaped pieces of rib knit layered together to form a double thickness and incorporated into the body below the neck. The V is therefore a separate fabric component with its own edges and joining seams, rather than a shape indicated only by decorative stitching across the surface. The change from the main sweatshirt knit to the rib-knit insert is visible as part of the garment's construction.

Extended Flatseam at the Point of Each V Insert
The stitching at the lower point of the V insert has a distinctive arrangement. Instead of both joining lines ending symmetrically at the point, one side of the flatseam continues downward for a short distance beyond it.

This extension produces a stitch line resembling a lowercase "y." The visible continuation emphasizes how the insert is joined to the body and gives the neckline area the utilitarian stitching character associated with vintage athletic garments.

Set-In Sleeves with Single-Panel Sleeve Construction
The long sleeves use a conventional set-in construction. A shaped sleeve cap is sewn into each body armhole, establishing a defined attachment line around the shoulder and creating a natural transition from the shoulder into the sleeve.

Each sleeve is formed from a single fabric panel joined along its underside to create a tube. This under-sleeve seam closes the sleeve lengthwise, while the shaped upper section connects it to the torso. Together, these joins give the sweatshirt the clearly outlined shoulder construction of a classic set-in athletic sweatshirt.

Extended Double-Layer Rib-Knit Cuffs
The cuffs are made from separate rib-knit components. Each cuff is folded back on itself to form a double layer and then sewn to the end of the main sweatshirt sleeve, creating a substantial ribbed finish around the wrist.

The rib knit has more stretch than the body fabric. It allows the opening to fit comfortably around the wrist and respond to arm movement while helping prevent the sleeve end from spreading open excessively.

The cuffs are longer than those on a typical contemporary sweatshirt, covering a greater area around the wrists. This extended length helps limit the entry of cool air through the sleeve openings and contributes to the distinctive proportions of vintage-inspired athletic wear.

Extended Rib-Knit Waistband
The lower body is finished with a separately attached rib-knit waistband, proportioned with an extended depth that complements the long cuffs. Its broad band construction covers a greater area around the waist, while the stretch of the rib knit allows it to sit closer to the body than the main sweatshirt fabric.

The waistband helps hold the lower edge near the waist. Because the body fabric is roomier than the ribbed opening, a small amount of fabric gathers above the band, producing the gently rounded lower silhouette characteristic of classic sweatshirts.

The longer waistband is both a visual and functional detail. It establishes the sweatshirt's vintage-inspired body-to-rib proportions, helps stabilize the hem position, and reduces the open space through which cool air can enter from below.

Four-Needle Flatseam Construction
The major garment components are joined using a four-needle flatseamer. The resulting flatseams keep the fabric junctions comparatively level and reduce the raised seam allowances and localized thickness that can occur inside conventionally sewn joins.

This construction is used at major joining areas including the shoulders, armholes, under-sleeve seams, V inserts, cuffs, and waistband. Each of these areas brings substantial fabric components together, making the seam profile especially relevant to how the inside of the garment feels against the body.

Keeping these joins relatively flat helps control bulky ridges at the garment's assembly points. The sweatshirt can therefore retain the thickness of its extra heavyweight fabric while limiting the additional bulk created by the seams themselves.

Visible Stitch Lines That Outline the Garment's Construction
The four-needle flatseams are visible on the exterior as well as serving to join the components. Their stitch lines follow the boundaries between the body, sleeves, inserts, and rib-knit parts, making these construction changes visible from the outside.

This gives the garment a restrained structural accent in addition to its front graphic. The lines that shape its appearance are the working seams of the sweatshirt, so the stitching provides a visible expression of how the individual parts are assembled.

Felix the Cat "Strike Again" Bowling Graphic
The front features a bowling-themed Felix the Cat graphic. "FELIX THE CAT" lettering arches above the illustration, with "STRIKE AGAIN" placed below it. This arrangement frames the character image between the upper and lower lettering.

The combination of character artwork and lettering recalls the playful appearance of vintage printed sweatshirts. Set against the substantial cotton knit and visible construction details, the graphic adds a distinct focal point to the classic athletic design.

Print Character Across the Front V-Insert Seam
The front print extends across the junction between the V insert and the surrounding body fabric. In this area, the printed surface crosses both a seam and the change between the rib-knit insert and the main sweatshirt knit.

The differences in surface height and fabric texture result in uneven coverage and lightly broken or faded-looking areas within the print around the seam. These irregularities are an intended characteristic of the product's finish. Please be aware of this detail when viewing the graphic at close range.

Made in Japan
TOYS McCOY model TMC2643 is made in Japan. Its 14.8 oz. brushed-back cotton fabric, tubular torso, reinforced binder neckline, front and back V inserts, extended rib-knit finishes, and four-needle flatseams bring together the substantial feel and practical construction of classic athletic sweatshirts.

The relatively short body and moderately roomy fit retain those traditional proportions, while the Felix the Cat bowling graphic gives the design a playful point of interest. Together, the fabric, construction, and artwork create a vintage-inspired sweatshirt suited to everyday casual outfits.

The cuffs are made from separate rib-knit components. Each cuff is folded back on itself to form a double layer and then sewn to the end of the main sweatshirt sleeve, creating a substantial ribbed finish around the wrist.

The rib knit has more stretch than the body fabric. It allows the opening to fit comfortably around the wrist and respond to arm movement while helping prevent the sleeve end from spreading open excessively.

The cuffs are longer than those on a typical contemporary sweatshirt, covering a greater area around the wrists. This extended length helps limit the entry of cool air through the sleeve openings and contributes to the distinctive proportions of vintage-inspired athletic wear.

Extended Rib-Knit Waistband
The lower body is finished with a separately attached rib-knit waistband, proportioned with an extended depth that complements the long cuffs. Its broad band construction covers a greater area around the waist, while the stretch of the rib knit allows it to sit closer to the body than the main sweatshirt fabric.

The waistband helps hold the lower edge near the waist. Because the body fabric is roomier than the ribbed opening, a small amount of fabric gathers above the band, producing the gently rounded lower silhouette characteristic of classic sweatshirts.

The longer waistband is both a visual and functional detail. It establishes the sweatshirt's vintage-inspired body-to-rib proportions, helps stabilize the hem position, and reduces the open space through which cool air can enter from below.

Four-Needle Flatseam Construction
The major garment components are joined using a four-needle flatseamer. The resulting flatseams keep the fabric junctions comparatively level and reduce the raised seam allowances and localized thickness that can occur inside conventionally sewn joins.

This construction is used at major joining areas including the shoulders, armholes, under-sleeve seams, V inserts, cuffs, and waistband. Each of these areas brings substantial fabric components together, making the seam profile especially relevant to how the inside of the garment feels against the body.

Keeping these joins relatively flat helps control bulky ridges at the garment's assembly points. The sweatshirt can therefore retain the thickness of its extra heavyweight fabric while limiting the additional bulk created by the seams themselves.

Visible Stitch Lines That Outline the Garment's Construction
The four-needle flatseams are visible on the exterior as well as serving to join the components. Their stitch lines follow the boundaries between the body, sleeves, inserts, and rib-knit parts, making these construction changes visible from the outside.

This gives the garment a restrained structural accent in addition to its front graphic. The lines that shape its appearance are the working seams of the sweatshirt, so the stitching provides a visible expression of how the individual parts are assembled.

Felix the Cat "Strike Again" Bowling Graphic
The front features a bowling-themed Felix the Cat graphic. "FELIX THE CAT" lettering arches above the illustration, with "STRIKE AGAIN" placed below it. This arrangement frames the character image between the upper and lower lettering.

The combination of character artwork and lettering recalls the playful appearance of vintage printed sweatshirts. Set against the substantial cotton knit and visible construction details, the graphic adds a distinct focal point to the classic athletic design.

Print Character Across the Front V-Insert Seam
The front print extends across the junction between the V insert and the surrounding body fabric. In this area, the printed surface crosses both a seam and the change between the rib-knit insert and the main sweatshirt knit.

The differences in surface height and fabric texture result in uneven coverage and lightly broken or faded-looking areas within the print around the seam. These irregularities are an intended characteristic of the product's finish. Please be aware of this detail when viewing the graphic at close range.

Made in Japan
TOYS McCOY model TMC2643 is made in Japan. Its 14.8 oz. brushed-back cotton fabric, tubular torso, reinforced binder neckline, front and back V inserts, extended rib-knit finishes, and four-needle flatseams bring together the substantial feel and practical construction of classic athletic sweatshirts.

The relatively short body and moderately roomy fit retain those traditional proportions, while the Felix the Cat bowling graphic gives the design a playful point of interest. Together, the fabric, construction, and artwork create a vintage-inspired sweatshirt suited to everyday casual outfits.

Care Instructions
Hand wash gently.
Do not use chlorine bleach or oxygen bleach.
Iron on a low setting with a pressing cloth.
Do not dry clean.
Do not tumble dry.
Avoid strong spin extraction. Reshape after washing and air dry in the shade.

This is an unwashed 100% cotton garment. Slight shrinkage or other dimensional changes may occur during the first wash and subsequent laundering. Warm or hot water and tumble drying can increase shrinkage or cause distortion, so please avoid these methods. After washing, reshape the garment and allow it to dry naturally away from direct sunlight.

Always follow the care instructions attached to the actual product.

product.body_html:
Lee Men's Storm Rider-Inspired 101-LJ Heritage Blanket-Lined Denim Jacket, 13 oz Cotton Indigo Denim, Corduroy Collar, Relaxed Boxy Fit, One-Wash (LM5110-200 Deep Indigo Blue)

Lee (Lee Japan)

See available colors here

This men's blanket-lined denim jacket is made in Vietnam for Lee's Japanese-market collection and developed by EDWIN under license from The H.D. Lee Company, Inc., U.S.A. Its design draws on the lineage of Lee's 101-J Riders Jacket, the blanket-lined 101-LJ, and the later Storm Rider, bringing the recognizable construction and cold-weather character of these classic American denim jackets into a contemporary casual model.

The jacket combines a one-washed 13 oz cotton indigo denim shell with a brushed, striped wool-blend blanket lining through the body and sleeves and a contrasting brown corduroy point collar. A six-button front, zigzag-stitched folded plackets, angled chest pockets with curved buttoned flaps, sewn front darts, set-in sleeves with single-button cuffs, a multi-panel back, and buttoned waistband adjusters retain the characteristic details of the Riders Jacket design. Its roomy body and short length create a relaxed, boxy silhouette, while the lining adds warmth and thickness for use as an outer layer in cooler weather.

Size and Fit Guide:

When assessing fit, please allow for the lining as well as the thickness of the shirt, sweatshirt, or other layer you intend to wear underneath. Lee Workwear Heritage and the 101-J Riders Jacket
Lee was founded in Kansas, USA, in 1889 and has grown into one of America's best-known jeans and workwear brands. After its founding, the company began producing practical garments such as overalls, UNION-ALLS, and work jackets, and later developed numerous models closely associated with the history of American workwear and denim, including cowboy clothing, Lee COWBOY, the 101 series, RIDERS, the 101-J, 101-LJ, STORM RIDER, and WESTERNER. Today, Lee continues to produce denim-centered casual wear while incorporating functional details and construction rooted in traditional workwear.

The LM5110 is a men's blanket-lined denim jacket that carries forward the heritage of the STORM RIDER, one of Lee's signature insulated denim jackets. It combines a 13 oz indigo denim outer shell with a striped wool-blend blanket lining and a brown-toned corduroy collar, increasing insulation and warmth. The jacket is developed by EDWIN Co., Ltd., which operates the Lee brand in Japan, under license from The H.D. Lee Company, Inc., U.S.A., and is manufactured in Vietnam.

The design foundation of the LM5110 is Lee's iconic 101-J RIDERS JACKET. Developed from the earlier Lee COWBOY JACKET lineage, the 101-J became established as a distinctive denim jacket characterized by diagonally positioned chest pockets, two-line front darts, a short body length, and set-in sleeves.

From the Blanket-Lined 101-LJ to the Storm Rider
Based on the 101-J design, the blanket-lined 101-LJ appeared in the late 1940s as a version with increased cold-weather protection. While retaining the basic front design and body construction of the 101-J, the 101-LJ added an insulating blanket lining and adopted a corduroy collar in place of the denim collar, resulting in a warmer construction with greater insulation.

The 101-LJ was later offered under the STORM RIDER name, and the combination of a corduroy collar and striped blanket lining became established as one of Lee's characteristic insulated denim-jacket designs.

Contemporary Interpretation with a Secured Lining Hem
The LM5110 is not a vintage reproduction intended to faithfully duplicate every specification of a particular production year of the 101-LJ or STORM RIDER. Instead, it incorporates characteristic design and construction elements carried forward from the 101-J through the 101-LJ and STORM RIDER, reworked into a denim jacket suited to contemporary wear.

Certain early-1950s 101-LJ jackets used a free-hanging blanket-lining construction in which the lower edge of the lining was not sewn into the waistband, allowing some movement at the bottom of the lining. In contrast, the LM5110 secures the lower edge of the blanket lining into the waistband construction. Inside the collar, the jacket also features a label with the STORM RIDER name and artwork depicting a cowboy and a snowy landscape. Rather than reproducing an early 101-LJ exactly, the LM5110 incorporates features carried forward through the 101-LJ and later STORM RIDER while adapting them to a contemporary construction.

13 oz 100% Cotton Deep Indigo Denim Shell
The outer shell is made from 13 oz, 100% cotton deep indigo denim. The fabric retains a moderate degree of body and firmness while also offering a supple feel.

One-Wash Finish and Subsequent Shrinkage
A one-wash treatment is applied during the finishing process. This treatment eases some of the denim's initial stiffness, giving the fabric a more accommodating feel from the beginning compared with unwashed denim.

The initial wash also allows part of the fabric's early shrinkage to occur before sale, helping reduce the larger dimensional change normally associated with the first wash of an untreated garment. Some additional shrinkage may still occur depending on washing method, drying conditions, and repeated laundering.

Indigo Fading and Wear at Folds and Seams
With continued wear and washing, the denim gradually settles and develops variations in its indigo coloration. Areas exposed to frequent movement and friction, including the sleeve bends, front plackets, chest pocket areas, seams, cuffs, and hem, will gradually develop wear marks and lighter tones.

The fading and contrast that develop in the deep indigo denim, together with the changes that appear around the fabric and stitched areas, are characteristic of the garment's natural aging process.

Brushed Striped Recycled-Wool-Blend Blanket Lining
The body and sleeves are lined with a brushed striped blanket fabric made from a blend containing recycled wool. The lining combines multiple colored stripes and has the raised fibrous surface and irregular neps characteristic of a wool-blend blanket fabric.

The blanket lining helps create an insulating air layer inside the garment, increasing warmth and cold-weather protection.

Six-Button Front and Folded Plackets with Zigzag Stitching
The jacket has a full-opening front secured with six metal buttons. The front edges are turned inward to create a double-layer construction, reinforcing the plackets along the opening.

Lee's characteristic zigzag stitching is applied to the plackets. This stitching secures and stabilizes the doubled fabric while also creating one of the recognizable details associated with Lee RIDERS JACKET construction and classic Lee workwear. The buttonholes are positioned horizontally across the vertical front opening.

Brown Corduroy Point Collar without a Separate Collar Stand
The collar is made from brown-toned corduroy, creating a contrast in both texture and color against the denim body.

It has a classic point-collar shape and a standless construction, with no separate collar stand between the collar and neckline. The collar is attached directly to the neckline in a construction characteristic of traditional work jackets. Corduroy also provides a softer contact surface around the neck than denim, contributing to comfort where the collar comes into contact with the skin.

Angled Front Yokes and Rounded Chest Patch Pockets
The upper front is divided by yoke seams that rise diagonally from the center toward the sides, and the chest pockets are positioned in line with this angled construction.

Each chest pocket is an externally applied patch pocket with rounded lower corners and a curved flap shaped to complement the rounded form of the pocket body. A buttonhole is positioned at the center of each flap, allowing the flap to fasten over a button attached to the pocket body. A small Lee logo tab is sewn into the edge of the left chest pocket flap.

Sewn Front Darts for Body Shaping
Two-line front darts run from each chest pocket down to the upper edge of the waistband. These darts are formed by folding the body fabric inward and securing it with stitching.

The darts shape the front body three-dimensionally while emphasizing the vertical lines of the jacket and also serving as a visual design accent. They are not action pleats designed to open and provide additional range of motion; instead, they are a construction detail used to shape the front body.

Set-In Sleeve Construction
The sleeves use set-in construction and are attached to the body along defined shoulder seams.

Single-Button Cuffs with Sleeve Plackets
Each sleeve ends in a cuff with a single metal-button closure and a functional sleeve placket. When the button is released, the sleeve opening can spread wider, making the jacket easier to put on and take off.

Antiqued Lee RIDERS Metal Buttons
The metal buttons have an antiqued finish with a subdued brass-toned appearance. The face of each button is engraved with the "Lee RIDERS" name, adding a classic Lee workwear detail to the front closure, chest pockets, and cuffs.

Back Yoke and Multi-Panel Body Construction
The upper back is divided by a separate back yoke. Below the yoke, a large center-back panel is joined to side panels on the left and right, creating a multi-panel body construction.

The vertical panel seams help shape the back of the jacket and define its rear construction.

Rear Waistband Adjusters with Plastic Cat's-Eye Buttons
Adjustment tabs are positioned at the left and right sides of the rear waistband. One end of each tab is permanently sewn to the jacket, while the opposite end has a buttonhole and fastens to plastic cat's-eye buttons.

Under normal conditions, the tab is held at the outer button position. Moving it to the inner button position draws in the waistband, allowing the waist area to be tightened.

Storm Rider Label inside the Collar
Inside the collar, a brand label featuring the STORM RIDER name and graphic artwork is sewn into the jacket.

Made in Vietnam for Lee's Japanese-Market Collection
The jacket is developed by EDWIN Co., Ltd., which operates the Lee brand in Japan, under license from The H.D. Lee Company, Inc., U.S.A., and is manufactured in Vietnam.

The LM5110 is based on Lee's iconic 101-J RIDERS JACKET and incorporates characteristic elements developed through the blanket-lined 101-LJ and the later STORM RIDER, including the corduroy collar and blanket lining. These established Lee details are brought together in a contemporary model intended for everyday wear.

Care Instructions
- Machine wash on a gentle cycle at a maximum water temperature of 40°C / 104°F.
- Do not use chlorine bleach or oxygen bleach.
- Do not tumble dry.
- Hang to dry in the shade.
- Iron with a pressing cloth at a maximum soleplate temperature of 150°C / 302°F.
- Do not dry clean.
- Professional wet cleaning using a very gentle process is permitted.

The garment has been washed once during finishing. Some additional shrinkage may still occur depending on the washing method, drying conditions, and repeated laundering. Please always follow the care instructions attached to the actual product.

Due to the nature of indigo-dyed products, dye may transfer to other clothing, bags, furniture, or other surfaces through friction during wear or when the garment becomes damp from perspiration or rain. Please take particular care when wearing the jacket with white or light-colored clothing or using it near light-colored items.

Wash separately from other garments, as indigo dye may be released during laundering. To help prevent discoloration, do not use bleach or detergents containing bleaching agents. Prolonged exposure to sunlight or artificial lighting may also cause discoloration or fading, so please take care when storing the garment.

Important Notes

product.title: TOYS McCOY Men's Steve McQueen "The Great Escape" Reproduction Chino Pants, Military Trousers, 12.5 oz. Cotton Twill, Slim Straight Fit, Button Fly, Made in Japan (TMP2604, 040 Khaki)
product.body_html:
TOYS McCOY Men's Steve McQueen "The Great Escape" Reproduction Chino Pants, Military Trousers, 12.5 oz. Cotton Twill, Slim Straight Fit, Button Fly, Made in Japan (TMP2604, 040 Khaki)

TOYS McCOY

These men's khaki chino trousers are made in Japan by TOYS McCOY as a reproduction of the screen costume worn by Steve McQueen as Captain Virgil Hilts in The Great Escape. The design takes U.S. military chino trousers as its foundation while focusing specifically on the slimmer proportions, distinctive cut, and details of the trousers prepared for McQueen's appearance in the film. Unlike the roomier, utility-oriented silhouettes commonly associated with U.S. military chino trousers of the World War II era, the trousers seen on McQueen in the film are said to have been modified at his request for a cleaner, more streamlined appearance. For this reason, this model is not intended as a direct reproduction of a particular period-issued military specification. Instead, it recreates the screen costume itself, which was based on U.S. military chinos but altered to suit McQueen's preferred silhouette and the visual requirements of the film. TOYS McCOY has reconstructed these characteristics in a modern reproduction by considering the differences in silhouette from conventional military chinos, together with the texture and khaki tone of the fabric, button-fly front, pocket construction, and other period-inspired details. The flat front, mid rise, and slim straight legs combine the distinctive character of McQueen's screen-worn trousers with the practical construction of classic chino trousers, resulting in a style that remains highly wearable for contemporary casual use.

Size and Fit Guide:

Gender: Men.

Our model is wearing a tagged size 30. He is 5'9" (175 cm) tall, weighs approximately 130 lbs (59 kg), and has a chest measurement of approximately 36" (91 cm). His usual jeans size is 29.

Fit: These trousers have a slim straight fit, a standard mid rise, a flat front without pleats, and a button-fly closure. The seat and thighs have a more streamlined shape than traditional wide military chinos, while retaining room for everyday movement. The legs narrow very gently from the knees to the hems, maintaining a natural straight-leg appearance without a pronounced taper. The fabric has been one-washed to reduce initial shrinkage and ease its initial stiffness.

The actual waist measurements tend to run smaller than the tagged sizes suggest. If you prefer a little extra room at the waist, you may wish to consider one tagged size up as a starting point. Because the rise and waistband position affect how trousers fit, please measure a similar pair of chino pants that fits you well and compare the waist, front rise, thigh, and leg opening measurements before choosing your size.

Made in Japan.

- All measurements are taken by hand with the garment laid flat.
- Slight differences may occur between individual garments and measuring methods.
- Actual color may differ slightly from the photographs due to lighting and display settings.

Steve McQueen V. Hilts Screen-Costume Reproduction
These trousers reproduce the khaki pants worn by Steve McQueen in his role as Captain Virgil Hilts in The Great Escape. The costume trousers are said to have been altered at McQueen's request to create slimmer, cleaner proportions than the practical, wider silhouettes commonly associated with World War II U.S. military chinos.

The reproduction focuses on that modified screen costume rather than a single military-issued trouser pattern or a specific military specification. TOYS McCOY brings together the distinctive silhouette, closely woven fabric, subdued khaki color, button fly, pocket construction, and interior costume markings to reproduce the character of the trousers seen in the film.

Flat Front, Mid Rise, and Slim Straight Legs
The front is cut without pleats, keeping the fabric relatively flat across the upper front. A standard mid rise places the waistband neither unusually low nor especially high. The seat and thighs are shaped with less volume than traditional wide military chinos, creating a slimmer profile through the upper legs.

From the knees to the hems, the legs narrow only very gently. This slight reduction in width preserves a natural straight-leg line instead of producing a strongly tapered leg opening. The cut retains space for normal movement and is not intended to fit closely against the body like a skinny silhouette.

The resulting balance reflects the streamlined proportions of the film costume while retaining the practical ease of everyday trousers. The flat front and restrained leg shape allow the texture and color of the chino cloth to remain central to the overall appearance.

12.5 oz. 100% Cotton Chino Twill
The main fabric is 12.5 oz. chino cloth woven from 100% cotton. Its twill structure produces fine diagonal ribs across the surface. These closely spaced ribs are combined with a dense weave, giving the fabric a compact feel and a noticeable degree of body and resilience.

The cloth has enough firmness to support the shape of the trousers while remaining supple enough to bend with the wearer. This balance of structure and flexibility preserves the practical character of military-style chinos without making the fabric feel uniformly rigid.

The light, subdued khaki shade reflects the appearance of the movie costume. Fine twill definition and a closely woven surface give the fabric a clean appearance while retaining the substantial character of military trouser cloth. It is neither an extremely thin fabric nor a thick winter-specific cloth, making it suitable for casual wear across an extended portion of the year.

One-Wash Finish and Changes Through Wear
The trousers receive a one-wash treatment during finishing. Washing relaxes some of the initial stiffness of the densely woven chino cloth, making it easier to wear from the beginning while preserving the fabric's underlying body.

Because the garment has already been washed during production, the potential for substantial shrinkage after purchase is reduced compared with an unwashed garment. This does not mean the fabric is completely shrink-free. A small amount of further shrinkage may occur depending on the washing method and drying conditions.

With repeated wear and washing, the cotton fabric gradually becomes softer and more familiar to the wearer's movements. The fine twill surface also develops subtle changes in appearance as the cloth relaxes and is handled through everyday use.

Five-Button Fly with Four-Hole Urea Buttons
The front opening uses a traditional button fly comprising one top button at the waistband and four additional buttons inside the fly, for a total of five. The lower buttons are concealed within the fly construction when the trousers are fastened.

The buttons are made from urea resin and have four sewing holes. Their color coordinates with the khaki outer fabric, keeping the fastenings visually integrated with the trousers. The waistband button closes the top of the opening, while the four lower buttons secure the fly at successive points below it.

Separately Secured Buttonhole Sections
Below the top waistband buttonhole, the buttonhole side of the fly is secured with short stitches positioned between the individual buttonholes. These stitches divide the fly into separate sections, each containing one buttonhole.

This construction holds the fly layers together at intervals between the fastenings rather than leaving the entire buttonhole strip unsecured between its ends. The short securing stitches are a distinct construction detail within the concealed front opening.

Slanted Front Hand Pockets
The trousers have five pockets in total. Two hand pockets are positioned at the front, with their openings set at a diagonal on the left and right sides. The slanted entry follows a natural angle for inserting the hand.

The diagonal openings sit alongside the unpleated front, providing practical access without interrupting the overall flat-front arrangement. The pocket bags are contained inside the trousers.

Single-Welt Coin or Watch Pocket
A small horizontal pocket is set into the upper right front. Its opening is finished with a single welt, creating a narrow, defined edge at the entrance.

The compact pocket can be used for coins, a watch, or similarly small items. Its inset construction keeps the storage compartment inside the garment while presenting a discreet horizontal opening on the outside.

Single-Welt Inset Back Pockets
Two back pockets are positioned horizontally, one on each side of the rear. Each opening uses a single-welt construction, giving the pocket entrance a narrow, clearly defined finish.

The pocket bags are housed inside the trousers. Unlike an external patch pocket, this inset arrangement leaves only the welt and opening visible on the outside, maintaining a clean rear surface while providing accessible storage.

Off-White Cotton Drill Pocket Bags and Waistband Reinforcement
The front and rear pocket bags are made from off-white cotton drill with a tone close to natural ecru. Drill is a sturdy woven cotton fabric with a diagonal twill structure, making it a practical material for pocket interiors that repeatedly come into contact with hands and stored items.

The same off-white drill is used as reinforcement on the inside of the waistband. This additional fabric supports the inner waistband construction and creates a consistent interior finish alongside the pocket bags. Its lighter shade also distinguishes these internal components from the khaki outer cloth.

Interior Size Stamp and Costume Name Label
The inside of the waistband carries a size stamp and a costume name label. The label includes the wording "Toys McCoy Costume Co. Hollywood," Steve McQueen's name, and spaces for waist and inseam information.

These markings reproduce the name and sizing details associated with McQueen's trousers. Although hidden during normal wear, they reinforce the garment's identity as a reproduction of a film costume and extend that reference into the interior construction.

The entries "WAIST 32" and "INSEAM 31" are reproduced costume details associated with Steve McQueen's pants size. They are not the size designation or actual measurements of this garment. Please use the product's tagged size and the actual measurement charts when selecting your size.

Seven Belt Loops with an Offset Rear Loop
Seven relatively narrow belt loops are attached around the waistband. Their slim proportions keep the loops visually restrained while allowing a belt to be supported at multiple positions around the waist.

The loop near the center back is placed slightly to the left of the rear center seam. The rear seam and its allowances already create an area of overlapping fabric. Moving the loop away from that point is understood to avoid adding the loop's thickness directly over the existing layers, reflecting a practical approach to managing bulk during construction.

Tonal Stitching and Reinforced Attachment Points
The sewing thread is predominantly tonal, blending with the khaki fabric. Stitching around the pocket openings, fly, waistband, and belt loops defines these components without creating excessive contrast against the main cloth.

Reinforcement stitches are used at points that receive concentrated stress during wear and movement, including the ends of pocket openings and the attachment points of belt loops. These additional stitches support the areas where repeated pulling and handling place greater demands on the sewn construction.

Overlocked Inseam Allowances
Inside the legs, the edges of the inseam allowances are finished with overlock stitching. The stitches wrap around the exposed fabric edges to help contain the cut yarns and limit fraying.

This is an internal edge finish at the inseam. It keeps the seam allowances more securely contained in an area repeatedly exposed to movement and contact during wear.

Deep Turned Hems with Single-Row Stitching
At each leg opening, the main fabric is turned inward by a relatively generous amount and secured with a single row of stitching. The fold forms the finished lower edge, while the turned fabric remains inside the leg.

This construction adds a layer of the same chino cloth at the opening. The single row of stitching secures the turned portion to the leg while keeping the visible hem finish simple.

Made in Japan
These trousers are made in Japan as part of TOYS McCOY's reproduction of Steve McQueen's V. Hilts wardrobe. McQueen's screen clothing was shaped through adjustments to details such as shirt and jacket sleeve lengths and the width and balance of trousers, helping the costume suit both the character's movements and his appearance on screen.

This model brings that approach together through its slim straight silhouette, dense khaki chino twill, button fly, slanted front pockets, single-welt rear pockets, off-white interior components, and costume name label. The combination preserves the specific character of the film wardrobe within a practical pair of cotton chino trousers.

Care Instructions
Hand wash.
Do not use chlorine bleach or oxygen bleach.
Iron at a maximum soleplate temperature of 110°C (230°F), with a pressing cloth between the iron and the garment.
Do not dry clean.
Drip dry in the shade without spin-drying.
Do not tumble dry.
Although the trousers have been one-washed, slight additional shrinkage may occur depending on washing and drying conditions.
Always follow the care instructions attached to the actual product.

Buzz Rickson's Men's Type WEP Flight Jacket MIL-S-18342C U.S. Navy Reproduction BR15947 Olive

Buzz Rickson

This men's Type WEP flight jacket is made in Japan by Buzz Rickson's, Toyo Enterprises' military label specializing in reproductions and interpretations of vintage American military clothing. The jacket reproduces the later U.S. Navy WEP winter flying-suit configuration made to the MIL-S-18342C specification, commonly referred to as the C-Type and associated with the 1972 model. Its construction combines an Olive plain-weave nylon shell, a full cotton-canvas lining, a nylon-and-polyester pile interlining, a wool rib-knit collar and cuffs, distinctive V-shaped cuff-to-sleeve junctions, an action back for increased shoulder mobility, a SCOVILL-marked brass zipper with a horsehide pull tab, an internal wind flap, large flap-covered front patch pockets, a left upper-sleeve utility pocket, and a gathered fabric-covered waistband. Four internal attachment tabs reflect the jacket's original role as the upper component of a two-piece winter flying suit designed to connect with matching trousers. The pile interlining adds insulation, thickness, and volume through the body and sleeves, while the gathered waist and tapered knit cuffs help create the rounded silhouette characteristic of the later WEP design.

Size and Fit Guide:

The jacket has an insulating layer between the shell and lining, giving the body and sleeves noticeably more thickness and structure than lightweight-zone flight jackets such as L-2 styles, which do not use comparable insulation.
