Overall Product Character
This men's brown denim jacket is made in Japan by Studio D'Artisan and combines the construction of a classic early work jacket with two distinctive Japanese production techniques: low-speed denim weaving on a Toyoda GL-3 power loom and traditional Amami Dorozome mud dyeing. The jacket is constructed from substantial 15 oz. cotton denim woven from undyed ecru warp and weft yarns. After construction, the garment is dyed to create its earthy brown color.

The design is characterized by a short body length, vertically arranged front pleats, lower patch pockets, action pleats across the back, and an adjustable cinch-back strap. These functional details are derived from early workwear construction, but Studio D'Artisan has modified the overall balance and fabric specification to create a jacket suitable for contemporary casual wear.

This is an unlined, single-layer jacket. It can be worn as a light outer layer during spring and fall, over a T-shirt or lightweight shirt in milder weather, or as an intermediate layer under a heavier coat during colder seasons.

Silhouette and Fit
The jacket has a classic work-jacket silhouette with moderate room through the chest and torso, a relatively short body length, and a straight shape from the chest to the hem. It is not cut closely to follow the contours of the body, but it is also not designed with the substantially dropped shoulders or exaggerated proportions associated with modern oversized clothing.

The shoulder width is kept relatively natural, allowing the set-in sleeves to follow the wearer's shoulder line without creating excessive volume. The chest and body provide practical ease of movement, while the short length allows the hem to sit around the waist or upper hip area, depending on the wearer's height and body proportions.

The sleeves are designed with a standard length and a conventional set-in construction. The overall fit reflects the proportions of a vintage work jacket, providing enough room for layering while maintaining a controlled and balanced appearance.

15 oz. GL-3 Loom-Woven Denim
The jacket is made from 15 oz. denim woven from 100% cotton yarn on a Toyoda GL-3 power loom. The GL-3 was one of the earliest power looms developed in Japan and represents an important stage in the development of the Japanese textile industry.

Unlike modern high-speed weaving equipment, the GL-3 operates at an extremely low production rate. It is capable of weaving only approximately five meters of fabric per hour. This slow weaving speed allows the yarns to retain more of their natural irregularity and prevents the fabric from becoming excessively compressed or mechanically uniform.

Replacement components for the GL-3 are no longer commercially produced. Maintaining an operational loom may require usable parts to be recovered from other retired GL-3 machines. The limited availability of replacement parts, specialized mechanical adjustment, and low production efficiency make the continued use of this loom exceptionally labor-intensive.

The resulting denim has a firm, substantial hand with visible surface irregularity. Natural yarn thickness variation produces small neps, raised fibers, and uneven areas across the fabric. These characteristics are not manufacturing defects. They are inherent features of denim produced on early low-speed weaving equipment.

Studio D'Artisan Original Denim Specification
The denim was developed according to Studio D'Artisan's original fabric specification. The yarn count, yarn irregularity, warp and weft density, and weaving tension were selected to emphasize the distinctive characteristics of the GL-3 loom.

Both the warp and weft yarns are initially undyed ecru cotton. This differs from conventional blue denim, which is normally woven with indigo-dyed warp yarns and undyed weft yarns. By beginning with an entirely ecru denim base, the finished fabric can absorb the Amami Dorozome dye across both sets of yarns, producing a brown color that extends throughout the structure of the cloth.

The combination of irregular yarns, low-speed weaving, and substantial 15 oz. weight gives the fabric a pronounced three-dimensional surface. The cloth is not uniformly smooth. Instead, it contains subtle changes in yarn thickness, tension, and elevation that become more visible as the jacket is worn and washed.

Amami Dorozome Mud-Dyeing Process
The jacket is dyed using Amami Dorozome, a traditional dyeing technique practiced on Amami Oshima, an island in southern Japan. The process uses dye extracted from the locally grown Techi tree, also known as Sharinbai in Japanese. Its botanical classification is Rhaphiolepis indica var. umbellata.

The wood and bark of the Techi tree contain natural tannins. These materials are processed to create a botanical dye bath, and the garment is repeatedly immersed in the solution so that the tannins can penetrate the cotton fibers. The garment is then treated with the iron-rich mud found on Amami Oshima.

The iron in the mud reacts with the tannins absorbed into the fabric. This natural chemical reaction darkens the material and helps fix the color within the cotton fibers. Repeated botanical-dye and mud-treatment cycles gradually build the final earthy brown tone.

Because the coloration is created through repeated interaction between plant-derived tannins, iron-rich mud, water, cotton yarn, and manual processing, the resulting shade is not mechanically uniform. Minor variations in depth, surface tone, and color concentration may occur between individual garments and between different areas of the same garment. These variations are characteristic of the traditional dyeing method.

The finished color has a natural soil-like depth that differs from the flatter and more uniform appearance commonly produced by conventional synthetic dyes. The brown tone also emphasizes the neps, raised fibers, and irregular texture of the GL-3-woven denim.

One-Wash Finish
The finished jacket has been washed once before sale. This one-wash treatment removes a portion of the initial shrinkage and softens the rigid feel of newly woven denim, allowing the jacket to feel more comfortable and easier to wear from the beginning.

Although the one-wash process stabilizes the fabric to a certain degree, minor additional shrinkage or dimensional change may still occur depending on water temperature, washing method, drying conditions, and frequency of laundering. Cold water and natural air drying are recommended to reduce unnecessary shrinkage and color loss.

Wear and Color Development
The mud-dyed surface will gradually change through repeated wear, friction, movement, and washing. Areas exposed to frequent contact, including the seams, front pleats, pocket openings, cuffs, elbows, collar edges, and waistband, may develop lighter tones and more pronounced surface contrast.

The raised portions of the irregular denim surface will generally receive more abrasion than the recessed areas. This difference in friction can emphasize the fabric's uneven texture over time. The resulting color variation will depend on how the jacket is worn, how frequently it is washed, and the conditions in which it is used.

Because natural dyeing does not produce the same perfectly uniform and highly colorfast surface as some modern synthetic dye systems, gradual color transfer and fading should be regarded as inherent characteristics of the garment.

Collar Construction
The jacket has a simple shirt-style collar without a separate collar stand. The collar is attached directly to the neckline rather than being mounted on a raised band.

This construction keeps the collar base relatively low and creates a flatter roll than a collar with a separate stand. The result is a compact neckline that is consistent with the direct and functional construction of early work jackets.

Five-Button Front Closure
The front closes with five metal buttons positioned vertically along the front opening. The buttonholes are sewn horizontally, a traditional orientation that helps the button remain seated against lateral pulling forces generated when the wearer moves the arms or expands the chest.

The front placket is formed by folding the denim back on itself to create a double-layer structure. This reinforces the button and buttonhole area, helps control stretching along the front opening, and provides additional resistance to distortion during repeated fastening and unfastening.

Vertical Front Pleats
Four vertical front pleats are incorporated into the front body, with two pleats positioned on each side of the front opening. The pleats run parallel to the button placket, extending from below the front yoke to the upper edge of the waistband.

Each pleat is formed by folding a section of the front-body fabric inward and securing the fold at three separate points with horizontal rows of stitching. This construction retains a controlled amount of additional fabric within each front panel.

When the wearer reaches forward, raises the arms, or expands the chest, the folded sections can open slightly to provide additional ease across the chest and front body. This helps compensate for the limited stretch of the substantial 15 oz. denim and reduces pulling around the button placket, armholes, and upper front panels.

When the wearer returns to a neutral position, the pleats settle back into their folded configuration. This allows the front body to maintain a relatively flat and controlled appearance without the permanent fullness that would result from a wider body pattern.

In addition to their functional purpose, the four pleats create pronounced vertical lines extending along both sides of the front opening. This construction emphasizes the elongated panel structure and distinctive appearance associated with early work-jacket design.

Lower Patch Pockets
Two patch pockets are positioned on the lower front body, one on each side. The pockets have an open-top design without flaps, providing direct access while maintaining a simple and functional appearance.

The upper corners of each pocket are reinforced with metal rivets. These locations receive concentrated stress when the wearer inserts a hand or carries an object inside the pocket. The rivets help distribute this load and reduce the possibility of the pocket corners separating from the body fabric.

The pockets are constructed from the same 15 oz. mud-dyed denim as the main body. As the jacket is worn, the pocket edges and riveted corners may develop visible abrasion and color contrast.

Set-In Sleeve Construction
The sleeves are attached to the body with conventional set-in armholes. Unlike a dropped-shoulder or raglan construction, the sleeve seam is positioned close to the natural shoulder point.

This construction gives the shoulder area a controlled shape and allows the sleeve to extend naturally from the upper body. It also helps preserve the structured appearance associated with classic work jackets.

Button Cuffs and Riveted Cuff Slits
Each sleeve is finished with a single-button cuff. A cuff slit is positioned above the cuff opening to provide enough space for the hand to pass through the sleeve and to allow the cuff to open during dressing.

A reinforcing metal rivet is installed at the upper end of each cuff slit. This point is exposed to repeated pulling and concentrated stress when the cuff is opened, closed, or pulled over the hand. The rivet helps reduce the risk of the slit extending or tearing into the sleeve fabric.

Black-Coated Metal Buttons
The front and cuff buttons are made from metal and finished with a black coating. Each button is stamped with the Studio D'Artisan brand logo.

The dark hardware coordinates with the earthy brown denim while maintaining a restrained industrial appearance. With extended wear, friction may gradually alter the surface of the black coating, particularly along raised edges and areas that frequently contact the buttonholes.

Straight Back Yoke
The upper back is divided by a straight horizontal yoke extending across the shoulders. This yoke supports the upper portion of the jacket and provides a stable structural transition between the shoulder area and the lower back panels.

Below the yoke, the back body is constructed from two panels joined by a vertical center seam. The center seam helps shape and stabilize the wide back area while maintaining the symmetrical appearance of the jacket.

Rear Action Pleats
Vertical action pleats are positioned on both sides of the back body. The pleats extend from below the back yoke toward the waistband area.

When the wearer reaches forward, lifts the arms, or moves the shoulders, these pleats can open to release additional fabric across the upper back. This increases mobility through the shoulder blades and reduces the amount of pulling transferred directly to the armholes, shoulder seams, and back yoke.

When the arms return to a neutral position, the pleats fold back toward the body. This allows the jacket to provide additional movement without requiring a permanently wide or oversized back silhouette.

Adjustable Cinch-Back Strap
An adjustable cinch-back strap is positioned near the lower back. The two ends of the strap are secured to the body with metal rivets, and the strap passes through a metal buckle.

Tightening the buckle draws in a portion of the fabric at the rear waistband, allowing the wearer to make a limited adjustment to the circumference and shape of the lower back. Loosening the strap restores more room through the hem.

The cinch-back is both a functional adjustment device and a characteristic detail associated with early workwear construction.

Please note that the exposed buckle and rivets may scratch or abrade surfaces such as automobile seats, leather or fabric sofas, chairs, painted furniture, and other finished materials. Care should be taken when sitting or leaning against delicate surfaces.

Leather Brand Patch
A Studio D'Artisan leather brand patch is attached inside the jacket at the back of the neck. The leather will gradually soften and change in tone with exposure to movement, moisture, body heat, and repeated wear.

Natural differences in grain, color, and surface texture may be visible in the leather. These characteristics are inherent to the material rather than defects.

Modified Vintage Work-Jacket Design
The jacket incorporates recognizable elements of early work-jacket construction, including a short body, low collar, vertical front pleats, riveted patch pockets, set-in sleeves, cuff slits, rear action pleats, a center-seamed back, and an adjustable cinch-back.

Rather than serving as a direct reproduction of one specific historical garment, this model combines these traditional construction details with Studio D'Artisan's proprietary GL-3 denim specification and the natural coloration of Amami Dorozome mud dyeing.

The result is a modified work-jacket design that retains the practical structure of vintage clothing while presenting a distinctive brown color and fabric texture developed through specialized Japanese weaving and dyeing processes.

Natural-Dye Color Transfer
This garment is colored with natural dye, and excess pigment remaining on or near the surface may transfer through friction. Until the initial excess color has gradually been reduced through wear and washing, the jacket should be kept away from light-colored clothing, bags, upholstery, footwear, and other items that may easily absorb pigment.

Color transfer may occur when the jacket is dry, but the risk increases when the fabric is damp from rain, perspiration, washing, or high humidity. Friction at the cuffs, underarms, waistband, collar, and areas that contact bags or seats may also cause pigment to transfer.

Do not place the wet or damp garment directly against other clothing or household surfaces. Do not leave the jacket soaking in water or folded while wet, as dissolved dye may migrate and create uneven staining.

Washing and Care Precautions
Wash this jacket separately from other garments. Use cold water and a mild detergent. Do not use chlorine bleach, oxygen bleach, hot water, or a tumble dryer.

After washing, remove the jacket promptly, reshape it carefully, and allow it to air-dry in the shade. Avoid leaving the garment wet for an extended period. Prolonged soaking or contact with other wet materials may cause dye to bleed or transfer.

Because of the natural dyeing process, some color loss is expected during washing. Variations in fading and surface color are part of the intended character of the garment.

Made in Japan
The jacket is made in Japan using Studio D'Artisan's original 15 oz. GL-3 loom-woven cotton denim and finished with traditional Amami Dorozome mud dyeing. Its fabric, construction, hardware, and functional details combine Japanese textile production with the practical design principles of classic workwear.


Toyoda GL-3 Power Loom

An Early Japanese Power Loom
The GL-3 is an early Japanese shuttle-type power loom manufactured by Toyoda Automatic Loom Works, now known as Toyota Industries Corporation. It was developed before the widespread adoption of modern high-speed textile machinery and reflects an earlier stage of Japanese weaving technology.

Only a limited number of GL-3 looms remain in operation today. Their rarity, low production capacity, and distinctive weaving characteristics have made them highly valued for producing specialized fabrics with pronounced surface variation.

Difficult to Maintain
Replacement parts for the GL-3 are no longer commercially manufactured. When a component becomes worn or damaged, usable parts may need to be recovered from another retired or non-operational GL-3 loom.

Keeping the machine in working condition requires experienced technicians who understand its mechanical timing, shuttle movement, yarn tension, take-up system, and other operating characteristics.

Small changes in alignment or mechanical adjustment can affect both the stability of the weaving process and the appearance of the finished fabric. Regular inspection, careful adjustment, and continued maintenance are therefore essential.

Extremely Slow Weaving Speed
A GL-3 can weave only approximately five meters of fabric per hour. This is considerably slower than contemporary high-speed looms designed for large-scale industrial production.

From a manufacturing perspective, the GL-3 is highly inefficient. It requires more time, closer supervision, and greater mechanical attention to produce a relatively small quantity of fabric.

However, the slow operating speed allows the yarns to be woven without creating the highly compressed, smooth, and mechanically uniform surface commonly associated with modern mass-produced textiles.

Why the GL-3 Is Called a "Phantom Loom"
The GL-3 is sometimes referred to as a "phantom loom" because very few operational machines remain, replacement parts are difficult to obtain, and the technical knowledge required to maintain them is increasingly specialized.

The term also refers to the distinctive fabric character produced by the machine. Depending on the yarn and weaving specification, the GL-3 can produce visible neps, slubs, uneven elevations, and subtle variations in surface density that are difficult to reproduce with modern high-speed equipment.

These characteristics are not manufacturing defects. They result from the combination of irregular yarns, low-speed weaving, carefully controlled tension, and the mechanical properties of the older loom.

Fabric Characteristics Produced by the GL-3
Fabric woven on the GL-3 typically has a substantial hand and a visibly irregular surface. Differences in yarn thickness, tension, and placement create raised and recessed areas throughout the cloth.

Small neps, slubs, loose surface fibers, and variations in texture may be visible. Neps are small groups of entangled fibers, while slubs are thicker sections formed within intentionally irregular yarns.

Rather than appearing perfectly flat and uniform, the surface contains subtle variations that become more noticeable under changing light and through continued use.

The exact appearance and hand of the fabric depend on the yarn count, yarn irregularity, warp density, weft density, weaving tension, and other production specifications selected for each fabric.

Craftsmanship Rather Than Production Efficiency
Producing fabric on the GL-3 requires substantially more time and manual involvement than weaving on modern industrial machinery.

The loom must be carefully maintained, weaving conditions must be monitored, and mechanical adjustments may be required during production. The objective is not maximum output or complete visual uniformity, but the creation of fabric with controlled irregularity and distinctive surface character.

Each length of fabric reflects the interaction between the loom, the yarn specification, the mechanical settings, and the judgment of the loom operator.

The GL-3 therefore represents a production method that prioritizes fabric character, technical skill, and careful small-scale manufacturing over speed and efficiency.

Handling Amami Dorozome Mud-Dyed Products

Traditional Amami Dorozome Dyeing
Amami Dorozome is a traditional mud-dyeing method practiced on Amami Oshima in southern Japan.

The process uses a botanical dye extracted from the Techi tree, also known in Japanese as Sharinbai. The wood and bark contain natural tannins that can bond with textile fibers and react with iron.

The material is repeatedly immersed in the plant-based dye solution so that the tannins penetrate the fibers. It is then treated with iron-rich mud from Amami Oshima.

The iron in the mud reacts with the tannins and gradually deepens and fixes the color. Multiple dyeing and mud-treatment cycles are required to build the characteristic earthy tone.

Natural Color Variation
Amami Dorozome does not produce the mechanically uniform appearance associated with conventional synthetic dyeing.

Minor differences in color depth, concentration, and surface tone may occur between individual products. Subtle variations may also be visible within different areas of the same product.

Seams, folds, reinforced areas, and sections containing multiple layers of fabric may absorb or retain the dye differently from single-layer areas.

These variations are inherent characteristics of the traditional dyeing process and should not be regarded as defects.

Color Transfer Through Friction
Natural dye remaining on or near the surface may transfer to other materials through friction.

Particular care should be taken when a mud-dyed product comes into contact with white or light-colored clothing, bags, shoes, furniture, automobile seats, upholstery, or other finished surfaces.

Areas exposed to repeated rubbing may release color more readily. Color transfer is often more noticeable during the early period of use, although it may continue depending on moisture, friction, and washing conditions.

Color Transfer When Wet or Damp
Moisture can increase the possibility of dye transfer. Perspiration, rain, washing water, humidity, or other sources of moisture may cause the surface dye to become more mobile.

When the product is damp, avoid direct contact with light-colored clothing, bags, furniture, car seats, and other materials that may absorb the dye.

Do not leave the wet product folded, compressed, or placed against another item for an extended period. Prolonged contact while wet may result in color transfer, uneven staining, or migration of dye between different sections.

Washing Instructions
Wash mud-dyed products separately from other items because released dye may transfer during washing.

When appropriate for the product, turn it inside out before washing. This reduces direct abrasion against the dyed outer surface and may help limit unnecessary surface color loss.

Use cold or lukewarm water, a mild detergent, and a gentle washing method. Avoid excessive mechanical agitation, scrubbing, brushing, or concentrated rubbing.

Do not use chlorine bleach or oxygen bleach. Avoid hot water and tumble drying unless specifically permitted by the care label attached to the product.

After washing, remove the product promptly, reshape it carefully, and allow it to air-dry naturally in the shade. Do not leave it soaking or wet for an extended period.

Always follow the specific care instructions provided on the product label.

Drying and Sunlight Precautions
When appropriate, turn the product inside out before drying and place it in a well-ventilated shaded area.

Avoid prolonged exposure to direct sunlight. Strong ultraviolet light may cause natural dyes to fade, discolor, or change unevenly, particularly when the product remains exposed in the same position for an extended period.

Direct sunlight should not be used intentionally to darken or develop the color, as it may instead cause unwanted or uneven fading.

Natural Aging and Color Development
The color and surface appearance of Amami Dorozome products will gradually change through use, friction, washing, moisture, and exposure to air.

Areas that receive frequent contact may become lighter, while recessed or less exposed areas may retain a darker tone. The resulting appearance will vary according to how the product is used, cleaned, dried, and stored.

No two naturally dyed products will develop in exactly the same manner.

Characteristics of Natural Dye
Color fading, surface variation, and occasional color transfer are inherent characteristics of Amami Dorozome and other natural dyeing methods.

These properties differ from the high degree of color uniformity and colorfastness commonly associated with modern synthetic dyes.

Careful handling can reduce unwanted transfer and uneven fading, but it cannot completely prevent the natural color from changing over time.

Please handle Amami Dorozome products with appropriate care and enjoy the individual color development and surface character created through continued use.
Care Instructions
Machine wash on a gentle cycle at a maximum water temperature of 40°C (104°F).
Do not use chlorine bleach or oxygen bleach.
Iron at a medium temperature with a pressing cloth placed between the iron and the garment.
Do not dry clean.
Due to the nature of the dye, color loss may occur. Wash separately from other garments.
Due to the characteristics of the fabric, slight shrinkage may occur after washing.
Color may transfer to other clothing, accessories, upholstery, or other surfaces through friction or when the garment is damp from perspiration, rain, or other moisture.

Important Notes

*Even after an order has been placed, an item may occasionally be sold out due to the timing of simultaneous purchases. We sincerely appreciate your understanding.

Overall Product Character:
- This men's long-sleeve work shirt is made in Japan by Sugar Cane, a workwear-focused label from Toyo Enterprises specializing in vintage-inspired American workwear. The design is based on the construction and practical character of classic American work shirts, combining a full button front, two functional chest pockets, reinforced seams, long set-in sleeves, and lightweight cotton chambray fabric. The red chambray gives the shirt a different visual character from a conventional blue chambray work shirt while retaining the straightforward, utility-oriented appearance associated with traditional workwear. Its balanced proportions and lightweight construction also make it suitable for regular use in a contemporary casual wardrobe.

Fabric Material:
- The shirt is constructed from lightweight 100% cotton chambray. Chambray is a plain-weave fabric traditionally used for American work shirts and is valued for its breathability, ease of movement, and lightly textured surface. Compared with heavier twill or denim fabrics, this chambray has a lighter and more breathable feel while retaining enough body to prevent the shirt from appearing overly thin or flimsy. The cotton fabric combines moderate crispness with natural flexibility, providing a lightly structured appearance without restricting everyday movement.

Red Chambray Weave and Yarn Character:
- The red chambray fabric is woven with red-dyed warp yarns and natural-colored weft yarns. This combination produces a mixed surface tone rather than the flat appearance of a uniformly dyed solid-red fabric. The natural-colored weft yarns show subtly through the red warp yarns, creating a softly mottled appearance with visual depth, fine color variation, and a slightly irregular character. This interaction between the differently colored yarns is a defining characteristic of chambray and gives the fabric a more natural and dimensional appearance.

Surface Texture and Hand Feel:
- The fabric surface shows slight irregularity, natural creasing, and a dry hand that reflect the character of the cotton yarns. It does not have an excessively smooth or mechanically uniform appearance. Instead, the fabric displays modest variations in texture and color that complement the vintage-inspired work-shirt design. Although lightweight, the fabric retains moderate firmness and body, along with the natural flexibility and comfortable hand associated with cotton chambray.

One-Wash Finish:
- The completed garment has been pre-washed, commonly referred to as a one-wash finish. This treatment helps reduce the initial stiffness of the fabric, gives the cotton chambray a more settled hand, and helps limit major shrinkage after purchase. Because the garment has already been washed during production, the fabric has a more natural drape and a less rigid feel than an unwashed shirt. Minor dimensional changes may still occur with repeated washing, depending on water temperature, washing method, and drying conditions.

Fit and Sizing Character:
- The shirt is cut in a classic work-shirt fit with moderate room through the chest and body. The silhouette is neither excessively slim nor overly loose, and the body falls relatively straight from the chest toward the hem. The proportions allow the shirt to be worn on its own, over a T-shirt, or beneath a jacket without creating an excessively bulky shape. The lightweight and breathable chambray fabric supports comfortable wear through spring and fall, while the long sleeves may also be rolled up during warmer conditions. This item generally fits close to standard U.S./EU sizing, but the actual garment measurements should be used as the primary reference because fit may vary according to body type and personal preference.

Collar Construction:
- The neckline is finished with a standard point collar attached to a separate collar stand. The collar stand supports the base of the collar, adding structure and stability around the neckline while helping the collar maintain its shape during wear. This two-piece construction gives the shirt a more structured appearance than an open-collar or camp-collar design and reflects the conventional construction of a classic button-front work shirt.

Front Placket and Button Closure:
- The shirt uses a full button-front closure for easy dressing and adjustment. The center front is constructed with a six-button placket, and the buttonholes are positioned vertically. The spacing between the collar button and the second button is slightly narrower than the spacing between the remaining front buttons. This arrangement helps prevent the neckline from opening too widely when only the top button is left undone. The placket also provides additional structure along the center front, where repeated buttoning and unbuttoning place stress on the fabric.

Buttons:
- Cat's-eye resin buttons are used throughout the shirt. This traditional workwear-style button is identified by its recessed center groove, which protects and guides the attachment thread while adding a subtle period-inspired appearance. The simple shape and practical resin construction complement the functional character of the garment without introducing unnecessary decoration.

Sleeve Construction:
- The shirt features long set-in sleeves. Each sleeve is shaped with a sleeve cap and sewn into the armhole along the shoulder and upper body. This construction creates a defined shoulder seam and a conventional shirt profile, in contrast to raglan or one-piece sleeve constructions. The set-in sleeve design provides a structured shoulder line while allowing the sleeves to follow the natural position of the arms.

Cuff and Sleeve Placket Construction:
- Each sleeve is finished with a single-button cuff. The outer corner of the cuff has a rounded profile, and the cuff buttonhole is positioned horizontally. A separate sleeve placket is incorporated into the cuff opening to provide additional room when putting on or removing the shirt and to allow the cuff to open fully. The base of the sleeve placket is reinforced with bartack stitching, strengthening an area that is repeatedly subjected to pulling and movement during wear.

Chest Pocket Design:
- Two button-flap patch pockets are applied directly to the front body. Each pocket is constructed with rounded lower corners, which soften the outline while retaining the practical appearance of a traditional work-shirt pocket. The separate flaps close with buttons to help secure small items and give the chest area a balanced, structured appearance.

Pen Slot Detail:
- The left chest pocket flap includes a buttonhole-style pen slot. This opening allows a pen or similarly shaped small item to be inserted without requiring the entire pocket flap to be opened. The detail reflects the utility-oriented construction of traditional work shirts, in which chest pockets were designed to carry writing instruments and small work-related tools.

Pocket Reinforcement:
- The upper corners of both chest pockets are reinforced with bartacks. Bartacking uses a dense concentration of stitches to strengthen areas that are likely to receive repeated pulling or stress. On patch pockets, the upper corners are particularly vulnerable when items are inserted or removed, so this reinforcement helps improve durability and maintain the stability of the pocket attachment.

Back Yoke Construction:
- The upper back is divided by a subtly curved shoulder yoke panel. The yoke is constructed with two layers of fabric, adding strength and dimensional stability across the shoulders and upper back. This area receives frequent movement during arm and shoulder motion, and the layered construction helps distribute stress while maintaining the shape of the upper body.

Hem Shape:
- The hem is finished with a traditional rounded shirttail profile. The front and back sections extend lower at the center and curve gradually upward toward the side seams. This shape provides additional coverage when the shirt is worn untucked and helps the longer front and back sections remain inside the waistband when the shirt is tucked in. Unlike a straight square-cut hem, the rounded construction gives the garment the conventional lower-body profile associated with classic work shirts and casual button-up shirts.

Triple-Needle Stitching:
- High-stress areas, including the shoulders, armholes, and side seams, are sewn with triple-needle stitching. This construction uses three parallel rows of stitches to reinforce seams that are repeatedly subjected to movement, pulling, and laundering. In addition to improving seam stability, the three visible stitch lines create the strong, clearly defined seam appearance commonly associated with traditional American workwear.

Contrast Stitching:
- Natural-colored stitching is used throughout the shirt. The lighter thread contrasts with the red chambray fabric and clearly outlines the pockets, front placket, back yoke, sleeves, cuffs, and major seam lines. The contrast is functional as well as visual, emphasizing the garment's construction and reinforcing its classic workwear character without relying on decorative embroidery or applied graphics.

Styling and Wearability:
- The lightweight red chambray fabric, long-sleeve construction, functional chest pockets, and reinforced workwear seams allow the shirt to be worn in several practical ways. It can be worn as a standalone button-up shirt, left open over a T-shirt, or layered beneath a jacket. The red chambray provides more visible color variation than conventional blue chambray, while the overall design remains straightforward and easy to coordinate with denim, chinos, fatigue pants, and other casual garments.

Brand Heritage:

Duke Kahanamoku was one of the most influential figures associated with Hawaiian culture, competitive swimming, surfing history, and the development of the Aloha shirt. Born in Hawaii, he achieved international recognition as an Olympic gold medalist and later played an important role in introducing surfing and the Hawaiian lifestyle to audiences around the world during the early twentieth century.

The clothing label bearing his name became one of the historically significant brands associated with the early development and popularization of the Aloha shirt. Particularly prominent from the late 1930s through the 1950s, the Duke Kahanamoku label became known for its distinctive tropical prints, relaxed silhouettes, and strong connection to the golden age of vintage Hawaiian shirting.

In Japan, Duke Kahanamoku garments are produced by Toyo Enterprises under official license from Malama Pono Ltd. Drawing from original garments, period catalogs, labels, textile samples, and other archival references, Toyo Enterprises develops both faithful reproductions of historically important Aloha shirts and original designs inspired by the brand's vintage heritage. These garments are produced with close attention to materials, construction, graphics, proportions, and period-informed finishing details, while maintaining the high manufacturing standards associated with Toyo Enterprises.

Historical Reproduction:

This model is a highly accurate reproduction of the vintage short-sleeve "Duke's Pineapple" Aloha shirt originally produced during the early 1950s. The reproduction is based on surviving archival examples and preserves the distinctive pineapple print, classic garment proportions, period-style construction, and vintage-inspired brand labeling associated with the original design.

Rather than simply applying a vintage-style graphic to a modern shirt body, Toyo Enterprises has recreated the garment as a complete historical design. Details such as the open collar, short and boxy body, straight hem, horizontal buttonholes, shell buttons, double-layer back yoke, back pleats, pattern-matched pockets, and archival-style woven neck label contribute to the historically authentic appearance of the finished shirt.

Fit and Silhouette:

The shirt is cut in a classic mid-century Hawaiian-shirt silhouette, with a generously proportioned body and a slightly shorter body length. The chest and upper torso provide ample ease, while the shoulders are shaped to allow comfortable movement without creating an excessively oversized appearance.

The straight-cut side seams and horizontally finished hem create a relaxed, boxy profile characteristic of vintage Aloha shirts from the period. Unlike a modern fitted shirt with a tapered waist and extended shirttail hem, this garment maintains a straighter shape from the chest through the waist. The shorter body length is specifically designed to be worn untucked and helps balance the wider chest measurement.

The resulting fit offers comfortable room through the chest, shoulders, and upper back while maintaining the compact proportions associated with traditional Hawaiian leisure shirts. Its relaxed construction also allows air to circulate more easily around the body, making it particularly suitable for warm-weather wear.

Open-Collar Construction:

The shirt features a traditional open collar constructed without a separate collar stand. This type of collar is designed to lie naturally against the upper chest and form a relaxed V-shaped opening when the top button is left unfastened.

When worn open, the collar creates the easy, informal appearance traditionally associated with Hawaiian shirts. A fabric loop is positioned at the collar edge and can be secured to the uppermost button when a more closed and orderly neckline is preferred. Fastening the loop button brings the collar points closer together and gives the neckline a more structured appearance.

Front Closure and Buttons:

The front is constructed with a full-length button opening and is secured by six buttons, including the button used with the collar loop. The buttons are four-hole white mother-of-pearl buttons made from natural shell.

Because mother-of-pearl is a natural material, each button may display subtle variations in color, luster, surface pattern, and translucency. Their restrained sheen complements the matte surface of the rayon fabric and adds a refined detail without detracting from the all-over print.

The front buttonholes are positioned horizontally across the front placket. This orientation is consistent with the construction specifications of the reproduced vintage design and also helps stabilize the buttons against horizontal tension when the shirt is worn.

Fabric:

The shirt is made from 100% rayon Fujiette, a lightweight woven fabric selected to reproduce the appearance and hand of vintage Hawaiian shirting. The material has a smooth yet slightly dry surface, a subdued matte luster, and a fluid drape that allows the garment to fall naturally around the body.

Unlike a stiff cotton shirting fabric, rayon Fujiette moves easily and develops soft folds and subtle surface variations during wear. These characteristics contribute to the relaxed appearance of the shirt and enhance the visual depth of the printed design.

The lightweight construction makes the fabric comfortable for warm-weather use, while its flowing drape prevents the generously cut body from appearing excessively rigid or bulky. Natural wrinkling may develop with wear, which is an inherent characteristic of the material and contributes to its vintage-inspired appearance.

Straight Hem and Untucked Styling:

The bottom of the shirt is finished with a straight, horizontally cut hem, sometimes referred to as a square hem or square bottom. This construction differs from the curved shirttail hem commonly used on dress shirts intended to be tucked into trousers.

The straight hem allows the shirt to hang evenly when worn untucked and reinforces its relaxed, box-shaped silhouette. The compact body length and clean horizontal hem make the shirt easy to coordinate with jeans, chinos, shorts, or other casual trousers without requiring the garment to be tucked in.

Double-Layer Back Yoke:

The upper back is constructed with a double-layer back yoke. A second layer of fabric is incorporated across the shoulder area to reinforce a portion of the garment that is regularly subjected to tension from arm movement and daily wear.

This layered construction provides additional structural stability across the shoulders while helping the upper back maintain its intended shape. The yoke also creates a defined transition between the shoulder area and the fuller lower back panel.

Back Pleats:

Four shallow pleats are positioned directly below the back yoke, with two pleats placed on each side. These pleats introduce controlled fullness into the upper back without significantly changing the external shape of the garment.

When the arms move forward or outward, the pleats can open slightly to provide additional ease across the shoulder blades and upper back. This construction improves mobility while allowing the shirt to retain a clean, balanced appearance when the wearer is standing naturally.

Pattern-Matched Chest Pockets:

Two patch pockets are positioned on the chest. Each pocket has a softly curved lower edge that complements the rounded forms within the pineapple print.

The pockets are pattern matched to the front body of the shirt. During production, the pocket pieces are individually positioned and cut so that the printed design aligns as closely as possible with the surrounding body panel after sewing.

This process requires more careful fabric placement than standard pocket construction. By visually continuing the print across the pocket edges, the pockets remain less conspicuous and preserve the uninterrupted appearance of the all-over pattern. Minor alignment differences may occur because of the fluid nature of rayon fabric and the individual cutting and sewing process.

Discharge-Printed All-Over Pattern:

The pineapple motif is produced as an all-over pattern using a discharge-printing process. In this method, the base fabric is first dyed, and selected areas of the dyed ground are then chemically discharged to remove or reduce the original color and form the printed design.

Unlike a surface print in which a thick layer of pigment sits on top of the cloth, discharge printing allows the design to become more closely integrated with the fabric itself. This results in a softer hand, reduced surface buildup, and a more natural transition between the printed motif and the background color.

The process gives the artwork a subdued, slightly irregular character that is especially appropriate for reproducing vintage Hawaiian textiles. Small variations in color density or tonal appearance are natural characteristics of this printing method and should not be considered defects.

"Duke's Pineapple" Design:

The printed artwork is based on "Duke's Pineapple," one of the most recognizable and historically important designs associated with the Duke Kahanamoku label. The composition combines stylized pineapple motifs, leaves, and supporting tropical elements in a dense all-over arrangement that gives the shirt a strong visual presence while maintaining a balanced overall pattern.

Pineapple designs occupy an important place in the history of vintage Aloha shirts, and "Duke's Pineapple" is among the best-known examples. The design became widely recognized in connection with the 1953 motion picture From Here to Eternity, helping establish it as one of the most celebrated pineapple patterns in the history of Hawaiian shirting.

Its lasting appeal comes from the combination of a distinctly Hawaiian subject, a strong mid-century graphic composition, and a color treatment that works naturally with the drape and movement of rayon fabric. The design remains visually expressive while retaining the refined character associated with collectible vintage Aloha shirts.

Pattern Placement and Individual Variation:

As a result, the position of the design on the collar, front panels, sleeves, back, and pockets may differ from the garment shown in the product photographs.

These differences are a normal result of the cutting process and make the pattern arrangement of each shirt slightly individual. Material characteristics, sewing, pressing, and finishing may also produce minor variations in the actual garment measurements.

This men's short-sleeve graphic T-shirt is made in Japan by TOYS McCOY, a brand renowned for its vintage-inspired craftsmanship and meticulous attention to detail. Part of the TOYS McCOY Hollywood Legend collection, this model is inspired by the “U.S. MARINES” T-shirt worn by Robert De Niro as Travis Bickle in the 1976 American film Taxi Driver. The graphic is applied to a circular-knit tubular jersey body with no side seams, combining classic graphic appeal with vintage-style construction and everyday wearability. Product Description

Fabric / Material

The body fabric is made from 100% cotton medium-weight circular-knit jersey. The garment is finished with a garment-dye process, also known as product dyeing or after-dyeing, which gives the fabric a naturally aged color tone and a slightly faded, vintage-inspired appearance from the beginning.

The jersey has a substantial medium-weight feel with enough body to give the shirt a solid presence, while still retaining the natural softness and flexibility of cotton. The fabric surface is not overly smooth or flat. Instead, it shows subtle vertical texture, fine yarn irregularity, slight slub-like variation, and faint nep-like character. These small surface variations give the fabric a more organic and dimensional appearance, helping the shirt avoid the flat, uniform look often associated with modern mass-produced jersey.

Although the fabric has a firm and substantial hand, it remains comfortable for casual wear. Through repeated wear and washing, the cotton jersey will continue to soften and develop more character, allowing the texture and color to age naturally over time.

Circular-Knit Tubular Body Construction

This T-shirt is made with a circular-knit tubular body. The torso is knitted in a tube shape rather than being cut from flat fabric and sewn together at the sides. As a result, the body has no side seams, creating the classic “tubular body” construction often associated with vintage athletic T-shirts, military undershirts, and older American casual knitwear.

Because there are no side seams along the torso, the shirt has a clean, uninterrupted body structure and a smooth feel against the skin. The absence of side seams also reduces side-seam bulk and friction, contributing to a more comfortable wearing experience. Visually, the tubular construction gives the shirt a traditional, old-style appearance while supporting a simple and natural drape through the body.

Garment-Dyed Finish

After the T-shirt is fully sewn, it is garment-dyed as a finished product. This process allows the dye to settle naturally into the fabric, ribbing, seams, and edges, creating subtle tonal variation and a broken-in appearance that cannot be fully reproduced by using pre-dyed fabric alone.

The garment-dye finish gives the shirt a muted, slightly faded color tone with a dry, vintage-like atmosphere. It also helps the fabric feel more familiar and comfortable from the start. Because the garment is dyed and finished after sewing, much of the initial shrinkage has already been reduced, helping the size and fit remain relatively stable after purchase. However, as with all cotton knitwear, slight natural changes may still occur with repeated washing and wear.

Fit and Silhouette

The silhouette is cleaner and more compact than many traditional American tubular T-shirts. It is designed with a slim body, a shorter body length, and shorter sleeves, giving the shirt a neat and balanced appearance. This trim, modernized fit helps the T-shirt work well as everyday casual wear while still preserving the character of vintage American military and athletic T-shirts.

Rather than having an oversized or boxy shape, the shirt is cut to sit cleanly on the body. The result is a refined casual silhouette with a classic feel, making it easy to pair with jeans, chinos, fatigue pants, shorts, or other heritage-inspired casual clothing.

Neckline Construction

The neckline is based on a classic crew neck and finished with binder-neck construction using rib fabric. Unlike a simpler collar construction where the rib is merely attached to the body, the binder-neck method wraps the cut edge of the body fabric with ribbing and secures it with double stitching.

This construction reinforces the neckline from both the inside and outside, helping reduce stretching, twisting, and shape distortion over time. It also gives the neck opening a more stable and durable structure, which is especially important for a T-shirt designed to reflect the functional character of vintage athletic and military garments.

Seam Construction

The shoulder seams, armholes, sleeve openings, and bottom hem are finished with single-stitch sewing. This restrained sewing specification gives the shirt a clean, simple, and understated appearance. Rather than looking overly modern or heavily engineered, the single-stitch finish helps preserve the quiet, old-style character of the garment.

The overall sewing is simple but carefully executed, supporting the shirt's vintage-inspired design without unnecessary decorative construction. This balance of plainness and precision is part of the appeal of TOYS McCOY's reproduction-oriented approach.

Print Construction

The chest graphic is printed with a slightly glossy, rubber-like ink. The print has a denser surface presence than a fully absorbed matte print, giving the “U.S. MARINES” graphic a strong visual character while still fitting naturally with the garment-dyed fabric.

A distinctive feature of this print is that it has been designed so the graphic can be faintly seen from the reverse side of the fabric. This is an intentional reproduction detail inspired by the way the T-shirt appears in Taxi Driver, where Travis Bickle wears the shirt inside out and the print shows through from the opposite side. The faint reverse-side show-through is therefore not a flaw, but a deliberate design element created to reproduce the film's visual atmosphere.

Taxi Driver Film Reference

The graphic design is based on the “U.S. MARINES” T-shirt worn by Robert De Niro as Travis Bickle in Taxi Driver. In the film, Travis Bickle wears a U.S. Marines T-shirt that refers to his background as a Vietnam veteran. In the memorable training scene, the shirt is worn inside out, allowing the graphic to appear in a ghosted, reversed manner through the fabric.

TOYS McCOY has recreated not only the graphic motif itself, but also the particular visual effect of the print showing faintly through from the reverse side. This gives the shirt a stronger connection to the film than a standard military-style printed T-shirt and adds a layer of cinematic and collectible appeal to the garment.

Non-Reversible Note

Please note that this T-shirt is not constructed as a true reversible garment. The reverse-side print effect is included as a design detail to reference the way the shirt appears in the film, but the shirt itself is not designed as a two-sided reversible T-shirt.

To support the film-inspired look, the size label is not attached at the back of the neck, but placed at the hem area instead. This allows the shirt to better reference the inside-out appearance seen in the film. However, the garment still includes care labeling and is fundamentally constructed as a standard single-face T-shirt. Please understand this as a film-based reproduction detail rather than a functional reversible specification.

Collection Context

This model is part of the TOYS McCOY Hollywood Legend collection, a series that reinterprets memorable garments associated with classic American film history through TOYS McCOY's reproduction-wear perspective. Rather than treating the design as a simple movie graphic, the brand applies period-aware fabric selection, body construction, dyeing, print treatment, silhouette balance, and finishing details to create a wearable modern product with a strong vintage and cinematic identity.

The result is a T-shirt that combines film culture, military-inspired graphic design, Japanese craftsmanship, and classic American casualwear references. It can be appreciated both as a collectible piece connected to Taxi Driver and as a well-made everyday T-shirt with authentic vintage-inspired character.

Overall Character

Product Description

Fabric / Material

The body fabric is made from 100% cotton medium-weight circular-knit jersey. The garment is finished with a garment-dye process, also known as product dyeing or after-dyeing, which gives the fabric a naturally aged color tone and a slightly faded, vintage-inspired appearance from the beginning.

The jersey has a substantial medium-weight feel with enough body to give the shirt a solid presence, while still retaining the natural softness and flexibility of cotton. The fabric surface is not overly smooth or flat. Instead, it shows subtle vertical texture, fine yarn irregularity, slight slub-like variation, and faint nep-like character. These small surface variations give the fabric a more organic and dimensional appearance, helping the shirt avoid the flat, uniform look often associated with modern mass-produced jersey.

Although the fabric has a firm and substantial hand, it remains comfortable for casual wear. Through repeated wear and washing, the cotton jersey will continue to soften and develop more character, allowing the texture and color to age naturally over time.

Circular-Knit Tubular Body Construction

This T-shirt is made with a circular-knit tubular body. The torso is knitted in a tube shape rather than being cut from flat fabric and sewn together at the sides. As a result, the body has no side seams, creating the classic “tubular body” construction often associated with vintage athletic T-shirts, military undershirts, and older American casual knitwear.

Because there are no side seams along the torso, the shirt has a clean, uninterrupted body structure and a smooth feel against the skin. The absence of side seams also reduces side-seam bulk and friction, contributing to a more comfortable wearing experience. Visually, the tubular construction gives the shirt a traditional, old-style appearance while supporting a simple and natural drape through the body.

Garment-Dyed Finish

After the T-shirt is fully sewn, it is garment-dyed as a finished product. This process allows the dye to settle naturally into the fabric, ribbing, seams, and edges, creating subtle tonal variation and a broken-in appearance that cannot be fully reproduced by using pre-dyed fabric alone.

The garment-dye finish gives the shirt a muted, slightly faded color tone with a dry, vintage-like atmosphere. It also helps the fabric feel more familiar and comfortable from the start. Because the garment is dyed and finished after sewing, much of the initial shrinkage has already been reduced, helping the size and fit remain relatively stable after purchase. However, as with all cotton knitwear, slight natural changes may still occur with repeated washing and wear.

The silhouette is cleaner and more compact than many traditional American tubular T-shirts. It is designed with a slim body, a shorter body length, and shorter sleeves, giving the shirt a neat and balanced appearance. This trim, modernized fit helps the T-shirt work well as everyday casual wear while still preserving the character of vintage American military and athletic T-shirts.

Rather than having an oversized or boxy shape, the shirt is cut to sit cleanly on the body. The result is a refined casual silhouette with a classic feel, making it easy to pair with jeans, chinos, fatigue pants, shorts, or other heritage-inspired casual clothing.

Neckline Construction

The neckline is based on a classic crew neck and finished with binder-neck construction using rib fabric. Unlike a simpler collar construction where the rib is merely attached to the body, the binder-neck method wraps the cut edge of the body fabric with ribbing and secures it with double stitching.

This construction reinforces the neckline from both the inside and outside, helping reduce stretching, twisting, and shape distortion over time. It also gives the neck opening a more stable and durable structure, which is especially important for a T-shirt designed to reflect the functional character of vintage athletic and military garments.

The shoulder seams, armholes, sleeve openings, and bottom hem are finished with single-stitch sewing. This restrained sewing specification gives the shirt a clean, simple, and understated appearance. Rather than looking overly modern or heavily engineered, the single-stitch finish helps preserve the quiet, old-style character of the garment.

The overall sewing is simple but carefully executed, supporting the shirt's vintage-inspired design without unnecessary decorative construction. This balance of plainness and precision is part of the appeal of TOYS McCOY's reproduction-oriented approach.

The chest graphic is printed with a slightly glossy, rubber-like ink. The print has a denser surface presence than a fully absorbed matte print, giving the “U.S. MARINES” graphic a strong visual character while still fitting naturally with the garment-dyed fabric.

A distinctive feature of this print is that it has been designed so the graphic can be faintly seen from the reverse side of the fabric. This is an intentional reproduction detail inspired by the way the T-shirt appears in Taxi Driver, where Travis Bickle wears the shirt inside out and the print shows through from the opposite side. The faint reverse-side show-through is therefore not a flaw, but a deliberate design element created to reproduce the film's visual atmosphere.

In the film, Travis Bickle wears a U.S. Marines T-shirt that refers to his background as a Vietnam veteran. TOYS McCOY has recreated not only the graphic motif itself, but also the particular visual effect of the print showing faintly through from the reverse side. This gives the shirt a stronger connection to the film than a standard military-style printed T-shirt and adds a layer of cinematic and collectible appeal to the garment.

To support the film-inspired look, the size label is not attached at the back of the neck, but placed at the hem area instead. Product Description

Fabric

The fabric is a 100% cotton 11-ounce lightweight blue denim. It is woven on a shuttle loom using rope-dyed indigo yarns for the warp and gray yarns for the weft. The surface shows subtle yarn irregularities, fine natural hairiness, and a slightly uneven texture that are characteristic of traditional denim fabrics. Because the gray weft yarns subtly show through on the face of the fabric, the denim has a natural heathered cast and a slightly dry, workwear-like appearance.

Unlike modern denim fabrics that are often produced for maximum uniformity and smoothness, this fabric has a more rustic and dimensional texture. The combination of rope-dyed indigo warp yarns, gray weft yarns, and shuttle-loom weaving gives the fabric a classic blue denim character with depth and visual variation. With regular wear, the indigo surface will gradually develop fading, contrast, and a more personalized patina, allowing the shorts to age in a way unique to the wearer.

The garment has been one-washed. This process helps reduce most initial shrinkage while giving the fabric a more comfortable and wearable hand from the beginning.

Fit and Silhouette

The silhouette is designed with a high rise and a relaxed straight fit, giving the shorts a classic workwear profile. The fit is neither overly slim nor excessively loose, offering a comfortable, balanced shape with enough room through the top block and thigh. The length falls around the knee, creating a practical knee-length proportion that is easy to wear in warmer weather while still retaining the appearance of traditional work pants.

Front Closure

The front is constructed with a traditional button fly. A total of five metal buttons are used, including the waistband top button. The top button features the SUGAR CANE brand logo, while the buttons concealed inside the fly are metal donut buttons, a detail commonly associated with vintage workwear and denim trousers. The button-fly placket is also carefully constructed. Each buttonhole section on the fly is separated by individual rows of stitching, reinforcing the placket and helping maintain structure around each buttonhole. This detail adds durability to a high-stress area while giving the front closure a more authentic, workwear-oriented construction. The result is a front closure that enhances the vintage appearance of the shorts while also providing a firm and practical build.

Pocket Construction

The pocket layout is based on classic workwear utility. The front has slanted hand pockets on both sides, shaped for easy access. Above the right front pocket is a shallow utility pocket with a top-opening design. The back is equipped with large patch pockets on both sides, providing practical storage capacity while reinforcing the rugged appearance of the garment.

The front pocket bags are made with cotton pocketing cloth, and the lower portion of each pocket bag is woven more densely than the upper portion. This denser pocketing is used in the area most likely to receive stress from stored items, repeated hand movement, friction, and the weight of small objects. By strengthening the lower pocket-bag section, the construction improves durability and abrasion resistance in a part of the garment that is usually hidden from view but important for long-term wear.

The back patch pockets also include reinforcement on the inside lower section. This reinforcement cloth helps support the bottom of the pocket, where stress, weight, and friction tend to concentrate. On the outside of the garment, this internal reinforcement is visible as a horizontal line of stitching across the middle portion of the back pocket. Although it appears as a subtle design detail from the exterior, it is structurally functional and reflects the practical construction principles of traditional workwear.

Tool Details

In addition to the main pockets, the shorts feature a tool pocket on the right leg and a hammer loop on the left leg. These details are derived from classic work pants originally designed for carrying tools and small work items. On this pair, they add both functional utility and visual authenticity, strengthening the rugged character of the shorts without making them difficult to wear as everyday casual clothing.

Labels and Vintage-Inspired Trims

The label and trim details are also designed with vintage workwear in mind. A SUGAR CANE brand label is sewn onto the left back pocket, while a cloth patch is placed on the right side of the waistband. A size tag is inserted into the seam below the right back pocket, adding another workwear-style detail to the rear view of the garment.

Inside the left back pocket, a union-style tag is sewn in place. This type of label is often referred to as a union ticket or guarantee ticket and is a detail commonly found on vintage workwear, work shirts, and denim garments. Historically, such labels could indicate a union-related manufacturing background or quality assurance. In modern reproduction clothing, they serve as a period-correct design element that helps express the atmosphere and historical context of earlier American workwear. On this garment, the tag is not merely decorative; it helps reinforce the vintage workwear concept of the piece.

Sewing and Reinforcement Details

The waistband is equipped with five belt loops. The outseams, inseams, and back rise seam are sewn with triple-needle stitching, a durable construction method often associated with workwear garments. The main stitching is done in a white-tone thread, which stands out against the blue denim and emphasizes the garment's workwear construction.

Green reinforcement stitching is used at selected stress points, including the pocket openings and belt-loop areas. These contrast reinforcement stitches add both visual character and functional strength to areas that are subject to repeated pulling, movement, and wear. The combination of white stitching, green reinforcement stitching, triple-needle seams, and reinforced pocket construction gives the shorts a detailed and authentic workwear finish.

A vintage-style flasher is attached to the right back pocket with staples. This flasher is intended as a removable store-display detail and should be removed before wear. Together with the labels, pocket construction, contrast stitching, and workwear hardware, it contributes to the classic Sugar Cane presentation and enhances the overall vintage-inspired appearance of the garment.

Summary

This pair combines the easy wearability of 11-ounce lightweight denim with the durable construction and practical details of traditional American workwear. Although designed as warm-weather shorts, the garment is built with attention to fabric character, sewing specifications, hardware, labels, pocket reinforcement, and utility details. With wear, the denim will continue to develop more depth, fading, and character, making these Sugar Cane work shorts a piece that can be enjoyed not only for their immediate comfort, but also for the way they age over time.

Tubular Jersey Body

This means that the body is knitted in a continuous tube-like form rather than being made from separate front and back panels sewn together at the sides. The inner raw edge is finished with overlock stitching to control fraying and keep the interior edge clean, while the folded hem is secured from the outside with single-needle stitching. This combination provides a neat interior finish, stable hem construction, and a clean, streamlined appearance that complements the vintage-inspired character of the shirt.

Stitching and Construction
The shoulder seams and armholes are reinforced with double-needle stitching for added durability. These areas receive regular stress during wear, so the use of reinforced stitching helps the garment maintain its structure and withstand daily use. The combination of tubular body construction, reinforced seam work, carefully applied rib-knit trim, internal neck taping, and clean single-needle finishing reflects TOYS McCOY's attention to both vintage-inspired detailing and practical wearability.

Closure
Pull-over style with no front opening or closure. The T-shirt is designed to be worn over the head, preserving the clean, uninterrupted appearance of a classic short-sleeve jersey T-shirt.

Pattern
Graphic print. The front and back are decorated with commemorative TOYS McCOY 30th Anniversary graphic artwork created by the brand. The print is designed to evoke a vintage aesthetic, giving the design an intentionally aged, time-worn appearance.

Graphic Print
The graphics are rendered with a vintage-style distressed print effect, giving them a naturally worn-in appearance similar to an aged vintage T-shirt. 30th Anniversary Artwork
The original TOYS McCOY 30th Anniversary graphics are printed on a vintage-inspired tubular body, creating a special commemorative design that highlights the brand's long-standing attention to classic American casualwear and vintage garment construction. Set-in sleeves. The sleeves are constructed separately and sewn into the armholes, creating a familiar, structured T-shirt silhouette with a clean shoulder line and natural ease of movement.

Sleeve Length
Short sleeves. The sleeve length is designed for everyday casual wear and pairs naturally with the compact body balance of the shirt.

Please Note
The graphic print has been intentionally finished to create a vintage effect. Variations in tone, subtle fading, slight shading, and natural irregularities in the aged appearance are intentional and contribute to the garment's authentic, worn-in look. Please understand that these details are part of the overall aesthetic of the T-shirt and should not be considered defects.

Hand Wash Only
Hand washing is recommended to reduce mechanical stress on the fabric, seams, and printed graphics. This gentle method helps maintain the natural hand feel of the cotton and prevents unnecessary abrasion that may occur during machine washing.

Do Not Bleach
Bleaching agents can damage cotton fibers and cause discoloration, particularly on dyed fabrics and printed areas. Avoiding bleach helps preserve the original color tone and overall fabric strength.

Cool Iron (Use a Pressing Cloth)
If ironing is necessary, use a low-temperature (cool) iron setting and always place a pressing cloth between the iron and the garment. This prevents direct heat contact, protecting the fabric surface, printed graphics, and stitching from heat damage, shine, or scorching. Ironing from the reverse side is also recommended for added protection.

Do Not Dry Clean
Dry cleaning solvents are not suitable for this garment, as they may negatively affect the cotton fibers, print quality, and sewn construction. Wet care methods are preferred to maintain authenticity and material integrity.

Dry in Shade
Air drying in the shade helps prevent color fading and fabric deterioration caused by prolonged exposure to direct sunlight. This is especially important for garments with vintage-inspired dyes and graphics.

Fabric and Construction Details:

This men's solid-color short-sleeve pocket T-shirt is made in the USA by Buzz Rickson, a vintage-inspired label from Toyo Enterprise specializing in American military garments and heritage styles. Constructed from tubular-knit 6.0 oz. cotton jersey made with ring-spun yarn, this T-shirt combines details associated with classic American athletic wear with the clean, practical design of a traditional pocket tee. The fabric has a substantial medium-weight feel while remaining soft and comfortable against the skin. Its subtly uneven surface texture gives the garment a natural, vintage-like character without compromising its everyday wearability. With careful attention to fabric, construction, and understated detailing, this T-shirt is easy to incorporate into a contemporary casual wardrobe.

Material and Fabric:
- This T-shirt is made from 100% cotton tubular-knit jersey weighing approximately 6.0 oz. The fabric has a substantial medium-weight character: it is noticeably more substantial than a lightweight undershirt-style jersey, but it is not excessively thick or rigid. The knit provides enough body to give the garment a defined appearance while retaining the softness, flexibility, and breathability expected from a comfortable everyday cotton T-shirt.

Ring-Spun Cotton Yarn:
- The jersey is knitted from ring-spun cotton yarn. In ring spinning, cotton fibers are drawn out and twisted together to form a continuous yarn. This traditional spinning method contributes to a soft hand, natural surface character, and a subtly textured appearance. Rather than creating an overly smooth or completely uniform surface, the yarn allows the cotton fibers to retain a modest degree of natural variation and light surface hairiness. These qualities complement the vintage-inspired character of the garment while preserving a comfortable feel against the skin.

Fabric Texture and Surface Character:
- The surface of the jersey has a restrained but noticeable texture. Fine vertical knit wales appear across the fabric, creating subtle depth and preventing the surface from looking overly flat. Slight irregularities, fine slub-like variations, and light surface hairiness can also be seen throughout the knit. These characteristics are intentionally described as subtle: the fabric does not have an exaggeratedly rough or heavily uneven appearance. Instead, it offers a quiet, naturally varied texture that recalls the understated character of vintage cotton T-shirts.

Tubular-Knit Body Construction:
- The torso is constructed from a tubular-knit body panel with no side seams. Instead of cutting separate front and back sections and joining them together along the sides, the main body is knitted as a continuous tube. This construction removes the seams that would otherwise run vertically along the sides of the torso. The result is a clean, uninterrupted appearance and a comfortable fit with fewer stitched areas in direct contact with the body.

One-Wash Finish:
- The garment has been given a one-wash finish during production. This initial washing process helps settle the cotton jersey and reduce the amount of major shrinkage that might otherwise occur after the first home laundering. As a result, the T-shirt can be worn with a comparatively stable fit from the beginning. Some additional dimensional change may still occur with repeated washing, particularly if the garment is exposed to hot water or machine drying. To help maintain its shape and measurements, follow the care instructions and avoid tumble drying.

Silhouette and Sleeve Construction:
- This T-shirt follows a classic short-sleeve silhouette with set-in sleeves. Each sleeve is attached around a defined armhole seam, producing a conventional shoulder line rather than the diagonal seam arrangement found on raglan-sleeve garments. The proportions are intentionally straightforward and restrained, allowing the quality of the jersey and the construction details to remain the primary focus. The overall appearance is clean and traditional rather than oversized or heavily stylized.

Collar and Neckline Construction:
- The neckline is finished with a ribbed crew neck using binder-neck and bound collar construction. In this method, the edge of the body fabric is enclosed within the folded collar rib and secured with double-needle stitching, creating a durable and structurally stable neck finish. In addition to its functional benefits, this construction also contributes to the robust appearance often associated with vintage-inspired athletic T-shirts.

Sleeve Cuffs and Bottom Hem Construction:
- The sleeve openings and bottom hem are finished with double-needle stitching. Two parallel rows of stitches secure the folded edges, reinforcing areas that are subject to repeated movement, wear, and laundering. On the interior, the raw edges are neatly overlocked, also known as serged, to help prevent fraying and improve long-term seam stability. This finishing method keeps the construction relatively flat and unobtrusive, allowing the jersey to retain its natural flexibility and comfort.

Pocket Construction:
- The left chest is fitted with a patch pocket made from the same cotton jersey as the body. Rather than using a simple square shape, the pocket is finished with a pointed lower edge, giving it a subtly defined five-sided profile. This modest geometric detail adds visual interest while preserving the understated appearance of a traditional American pocket T-shirt. The matching body fabric maintains a cohesive look and allows the pocket to remain practical without appearing overly decorative.

Closure and Overall Design:
- This T-shirt is designed as a simple pull-over garment with no buttons, zippers, or other closure systems. Its character comes from the quality of the cotton jersey, the tubular-knit body, the durable neckline construction, the reinforced hems, and the pointed chest pocket rather than from added hardware or decorative elements. The result is a versatile plain pocket tee with a vintage-inspired appearance and practical everyday functionality.

Model name: Buzz Rickson's by Toyo Enterprises Lot No. BR78711 / BUZZ RICKSON'S POCKET T-SHIRT.

Care Instructions:
Machine wash cold, gentle cycle.
Do not bleach.
Do not tumble dry.
Hang dry in the shade.
Do not iron.
Do not dry clean.
Gentle professional wet cleaning only.
